tutorial.en:
# Extreme Close Up

The video maintains an extreme close-up shot, consistently isolating a very small detail of the subject or scene. An **ECU** fills the frame with a tiny portion of the subject, such as an eye, a finger on a trigger, or a drop of sweat.

ECUs create **maximum intimacy and intensity**. They force the audience to confront a single detail with nowhere else to look. Sergio Leone's extreme close-ups of eyes during standoffs in [*The Good, the Bad and the Ugly* (1966)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly) are among cinema's most iconic uses of this shot size.

- Related: [Close Up](taxonomy:186)
tutorial.zh:
# 极近特写

画面始终保持极近特写，只呈现主体的一个极小局部。**极近特写**（ECU）用一只眼睛、一根扣着扳机的手指或一滴汗珠填满整个画面。

极近特写制造**极致的亲密感与视觉压迫感**，迫使观众无法回避地直视某个细节。莱昂内在[《黄金三镖客》(1966)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly)中对决双方眼部的极近特写，是影史上这一景别最经典的运用。

- 相关: [特写](taxonomy:186)

tutorial.en:
# Close Up

The video maintains a close-up shot, highlighting a distinct part of the subject or scene while still preserving some surrounding context. A **CU** typically shows a character's full face or details of an object filling most of the frame.

Close-ups are the workhorse of emotional storytelling, used to **capture subtle facial expressions, reactions, and intimate moments**. They create a direct emotional connection between the character and the audience. Alfred Hitchcock called the close-up one of cinema's most powerful tools for controlling audience attention.

- Related: [Extreme Close Up](taxonomy:187) | [Medium Close Up](taxonomy:191)
tutorial.zh:
# 特写

画面始终保持特写，突出主体的某个显著局部，同时保留少量周围信息。**特写**（CU）通常展示角色的完整面部或一个占满大部分画面的物体的局部细节。

特写是情感叙事的核心手段，用于**捕捉细微表情、即时反应和私密时刻**，在角色与观众之间建立最直接的情感通道。希区柯克称特写为电影中控制观众注意力最有力的工具之一。

- 相关: [极近特写](taxonomy:187) | [中近景](taxonomy:191)

tutorial.en:
# Medium Close Up

The video maintains a medium close-up shot, framing the human subject from the chest upward. An **MCU** balances **facial detail with enough body language** to show gestures and posture.

This is the standard framing for **TV interviews, news anchors, video calls, and dialogue scenes** where both expression and upper-body movement matter. It is close enough for emotional connection but wide enough to show hand gestures and the relationship between characters in over-the-shoulder setups.

- Related: [Close Up](taxonomy:186) | [Medium](taxonomy:190)
tutorial.zh:
# 中近景

画面始终保持中近景，取人物胸部以上。**中近景**（MCU）兼顾**面部细节与上半身肢体语言**，同时展示表情和手势。

**电视采访、新闻播报、视频会议和对话场景**的标准景别——近到足以建立情感连接，宽到足以展示手部动作和过肩构图中的人物关系。

- 相关: [特写](taxonomy:186) | [中景](taxonomy:190)

tutorial.en:
# Medium

The video maintains a medium shot, framing about half of the human subject. A **MS** typically shows a person from roughly the waist up, providing a **balance between character detail and environmental context**.

The medium shot is the most versatile and commonly used shot size in narrative filmmaking. It is wide enough to show blocking and body language, yet close enough to read facial expressions. Classical Hollywood filmmaking relies heavily on medium shots for dialogue coverage.

- Related: [Medium Close Up](taxonomy:191) | [Medium Full](taxonomy:192)
tutorial.zh:
# 中景

画面始终保持中景，取人物大约腰部以上。**中景**（MS）在**角色细节与环境信息之间取得平衡**。

中景是叙事电影中最通用、使用最频繁的景别，既能展示场面调度和肢体语言，又能读取面部表情。经典好莱坞电影中大量使用中景来展示对话情节。

- 相关: [中近景](taxonomy:191) | [中全景](taxonomy:192)

tutorial.en:
# Medium Full

The video maintains a medium full shot, framing the human subject from mid-thigh (or knee) upward. Also called a **cowboy shot** or **American shot**, this framing became famous in Westerns where it was essential to show a gunslinger's holstered weapon at the hip.

The medium full shot provides **more body context than a standard medium** while keeping the subject large enough to read expressions. It is used in **action scenes, fashion photography, and any scenario where the subject's stance or outfit matters**.

- Related: [Medium](taxonomy:190) | [Full](taxonomy:189)
tutorial.zh:
# 中全景

画面始终保持中全景，取人物膝盖或大腿中部以上。又称**牛仔镜头**（Cowboy Shot），因西部片需要露出枪手腰间的枪套而得名。

中全景比中景提供**更多身体信息**，同时主体仍然足够大以辨识表情。常用于**动作戏、时装拍摄以及角色站姿或服装至关重要的场景**。

- 相关: [中景](taxonomy:190) | [全景](taxonomy:189)

tutorial.en:
# Full

The video maintains a full shot, framing the entire body of the salient subject without showing excessive surrounding scenery. A **FS** contains the subject from head to toe with minimal extra space.

Full shots emphasize **physicality, body language, costume, and movement**. They are essential for **dance sequences, fight choreography, and any scene where full-body action tells the story**. In character introductions, a full shot reveals everything about a figure's appearance at once.

- Related: [Medium Full](taxonomy:192) | [Wide](taxonomy:193)
tutorial.zh:
# 全景

画面始终保持全景，完整展示主体从头到脚，不含过多周围环境。**全景**（FS）以最少的留白容纳主体全身。

全景强调**体态、肢体语言、服装和整体动作**，在**舞蹈、武打和所有需要全身表演的场景**中不可或缺。

- 相关: [中全景](taxonomy:192) | [远景](taxonomy:193)

tutorial.en:
# Wide

The video maintains a wide shot, consistently showing wide scenery or framing the entire body of the salient subject with ample background context. A **WS** (or **long shot**) shows the subject within their broader environment.

Wide shots establish the **spatial relationship between characters and their surroundings**. They serve as establishing shots, provide breathing room in editing, and allow the audience to absorb the full geography of a scene. Directors like David Lean and John Ford used wide shots of landscapes as visual poetry.

- Related: [Full](taxonomy:189) | [Extreme Wide](taxonomy:188)
tutorial.zh:
# 远景

画面始终保持远景，在充分展示环境的同时完整呈现主体。**远景**（WS）展示人物与其所处环境的关系。

远景用于**建立空间关系**，作为建立镜头或在剪辑中提供视觉缓冲。大卫·里恩和约翰·福特常用风景远景来营造视觉诗意。

- 相关: [全景](taxonomy:189) | [大远景](taxonomy:188)

tutorial.en:
# Extreme Wide

The video maintains an extreme wide shot, consistently emphasizing the vast environment over any subjects. An **EWS** (or **extreme long shot**) makes any human figures tiny against a dominating landscape or cityscape.

Extreme wide shots convey **scale, isolation, grandeur, or insignificance**. They are signature shots in epics, science fiction, and nature documentaries. The opening shot of [*Lawrence of Arabia* (1962)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_of_Arabia_(film)), showing a tiny figure against an endless desert, exemplifies the EWS's power to communicate the vastness of the world.

- Related: [Wide](taxonomy:193) | [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218)
tutorial.zh:
# 大远景

画面始终保持大远景，广阔环境占绝对主导。**大远景**（EWS）使画面中的人物显得渺小，被景观或城市全貌所吞没。

大远景传达**规模感、孤立感、宏伟感或人的渺小**。[《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》(1962)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_of_Arabia_(film))开场——一个微小身影置身无尽沙漠——完美诠释了大远景的力量。

- 相关: [远景](taxonomy:193) | [风景镜头](taxonomy:218)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Size Change

The shot size changes noticeably during the video. The framing shifts between different shot sizes (e.g., from wide to close-up) **within a single continuous shot**, rather than through editing cuts.

In-shot size changes create **dynamic visual storytelling without cutting**. A dolly-in from wide to close-up can build emotional intensity, while a pull-out from close-up to wide can reveal surprising context. These continuous transitions feel more organic than jump cuts and maintain temporal continuity.

- Related: [Shot Size Change (Large →Small)](taxonomy:195) | [Shot Size Change (Small →Large)](taxonomy:196)
tutorial.zh:
# 景别变化

景别在**单个连续镜头内**发生明显变化（如从远景到特写），而非通过剪辑切换。

镜头内景别变化创造**不间断的视觉叙事**：从远景推入特写可逐步增强情感张力，从特写拉出可揭示出人意料的环境。

- 相关: [景别从大变小](taxonomy:195) | [景别从小变大](taxonomy:196)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Size Change (Large →Small)

The shot size changes noticeably from a wider to a tighter framing. The camera or zoom moves in during the shot, transitioning from a broader view to a more intimate one.

This progression **builds emotional intensity, narrows the audience's focus, and creates a sense of closing in** on the subject. It is a natural way to transition from establishing context to isolating a key detail or expression.

- Related: [Shot Size Change (Small →Large)](taxonomy:196) | [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35)
tutorial.zh:
# 景别从大变小

景别在镜头内从宽画面明显收紧。相机推进或变焦推入，从全景逐步过渡到更紧密的构图。

**增强情感强度、收窄观众注意力**，营造逐渐逼近主体的感觉。

- 相关: [景别从小变大](taxonomy:196) | [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [推](taxonomy:35)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Size Change (Small →Large)

The shot size changes noticeably from a tighter to a wider framing. The camera or zoom pulls back during the shot, revealing more of the environment.

This progression **creates reveals, builds context, or generates a sense of expanding perspective**. A classic example is a close-up that widens to show the character is actually in a surprising or dangerous location.

- Related: [Shot Size Change (Large →Small)](taxonomy:195) | [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29)
tutorial.zh:
# 景别从小变大

画面景别由紧向松过渡。相机拉远或变焦拉出，揭示更多环境。

用于**制造揭示效果、补充环境信息或营造视野逐渐打开的感觉**。

- 相关: [景别从大变小](taxonomy:195) | [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [拉](taxonomy:29)

# Human Shot

A shot that primarily focuses on human subjects. The frame is composed around one or more people, making their actions, expressions, or body language the visual center of attention.

Human-focused shots form the foundation of narrative filmmaking, where **character and performance drive storytelling**. The specific way humans are framed (close-up for emotion, wide for context) shapes how the audience connects with the characters on screen.

- Related: [Non-Human Shot](taxonomy:220) | [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218)
tutorial.zh:
# 人物镜头

画面主要聚焦于人物，构图围绕一个或多个人展开，其动作、表情或肢体语言是视觉中心。

以人物为核心的镜头是叙事电影的基础——**角色和表演驱动故事**。

- 相关: [非人物镜头](taxonomy:220) | [风景镜头](taxonomy:218)

tutorial.en:
# Non-Human Shot

A shot that primarily focuses on non-human subjects. The frame centers on animals, objects, vehicles, food, architecture, or other non-human elements as the primary visual subject.

Non-human shots are essential in **nature documentaries, product cinematography, food films, and sci-fi** where technology or environment serves as a character. They also appear in narrative films as insert shots that draw attention to symbolic objects or environmental details.

- Related: [Human Shot](taxonomy:208) | [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218)
tutorial.zh:
# 非人物镜头

画面主要聚焦于非人物主体——动物、物体、车辆、食物或建筑等。

在**自然纪录片、产品摄影、美食影片和科幻片**中不可或缺。在叙事影片中也常作为插入镜头出现。

- 相关: [人物镜头](taxonomy:208) | [风景镜头](taxonomy:218)

tutorial.en:
# Scenery Shot

The video shows scenery or environment without focusing on any subjects. No distinct subject dominates the frame; instead, the **landscape, cityscape, architecture, or atmospheric setting** fills the composition.

Scenery shots serve as **establishing shots, transitional breathers, or mood-setting interludes**. They give the audience spatial context and emotional tone. In the films of Terrence Malick and David Lean, expansive scenery shots carry as much narrative weight as character close-ups.

- Related: [Extreme Wide](taxonomy:188) | [Wide](taxonomy:193)
tutorial.zh:
# 风景镜头

画面展示风景或环境，不聚焦于任何特定主体。**景观、城市全貌、建筑或氛围化的场景**填满画面。

用于**建立场景、过渡间歇或情绪渲染**，为观众提供空间背景和情感基调。

- 相关: [大远景](taxonomy:188) | [远景](taxonomy:193)

tutorial.en:
# Multi-Subject (No Focus)

The video features multiple subjects in focus, with no single subject standing out as dominant. Several subjects share the frame with roughly **equal visual weight**, and the composition does not clearly prioritize one over the others.

This framing is used in **ensemble scenes, crowd shots, group portraits, and documentary coverage** where the relationships between subjects matter more than any individual. It can convey community, chaos, or democratic equality among characters.

- Related: [Multi-Subject (Single Focus)](taxonomy:216) | [Many Subjects](taxonomy:221)
tutorial.zh:
# 多主体（无焦点）

画面中多个主体以大致**相同的视觉权重**共享画面，没有单一主体占据主导。

用于**群戏、人群场景、集体肖像和纪实拍摄**。

- 相关: [多主体（单焦点）](taxonomy:216) | [多个主体](taxonomy:221)

tutorial.en:
# Multi-Subject (Single Focus)

The video features multiple subjects, but one clearly stands out as the main focus. While several elements share the frame, **composition, focus, lighting, or placement** direct the viewer's eye to a single dominant subject.

This is the default approach in most narrative filmmaking: a character stands in a crowd, but depth of field or central framing isolates them. It allows filmmakers to **establish context while maintaining clear storytelling hierarchy**.

- Related: [Multi-Subject (No Focus)](taxonomy:215) | [Single Dominant Subject](taxonomy:222)
tutorial.zh:
# 多主体（单焦点）

画面中有多个主体，但其中一个通过**构图、焦点、光线或位置**被明确突出为视觉中心。

叙事电影的默认方式：角色在人群中通过景深或居中构图被隔离出来，**在提供环境信息的同时保持清晰的叙事主次**。

- 相关: [多主体（无焦点）](taxonomy:215) | [单一主导主体](taxonomy:222)

# Single Dominant Subject

A video that maintains a single or two dominant subjects throughout. The composition consistently centers on **one or two clearly identifiable subjects** that command the viewer's attention.

Single-subject framing is the backbone of **character-driven storytelling, portraits, product shots, and interview setups**. Maintaining a consistent subject allows the audience to build a sustained connection.

- Related: [Many Subjects](taxonomy:221) | [Framing Subject](taxonomy:224)
tutorial.zh:
# 单一主导主体

画面全程围绕一到两个主导主体构图，始终以其为视觉中心。

**角色驱动叙事、人像、产品拍摄和采访设置**的基础。

- 相关: [多个主体](taxonomy:221) | [有构图主体](taxonomy:224)

tutorial.en:
# Many Subjects

The video either shows three or more main subjects in clear focus, or shifts focus from one subject to another. Multiple subjects share visual prominence, and the frame accommodates their **collective presence or sequential attention**.

Many-subject framing is used in **group scenes, ensemble casts, crowd coverage, and multi-character interactions**. Managing visual attention across multiple subjects is one of the key challenges of composition.

- Related: [Single Dominant Subject](taxonomy:222) | [Multi-Subject (No Focus)](taxonomy:215)
tutorial.zh:
# 多个主体

画面中出现三个或更多主要主体，或焦点在不同主体之间转移。

用于**群戏、合奏阵容、人群拍摄和多人互动场景**。

- 相关: [单一主导主体](taxonomy:222) | [多主体（无焦点）](taxonomy:215)

tutorial.en:
# Framing Subject

The video includes one or more salient subjects in the frame at any point. At least one **identifiable subject** (human, animal, object, or vehicle) appears and serves as a focal point for the composition.

This is a broad classification distinguishing shots that feature identifiable subjects from pure scenery or abstract imagery. Most narrative and documentary footage contains a framing subject.

- Related: [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218) | [Single Dominant Subject](taxonomy:222)
tutorial.zh:
# 有构图主体

画面中至少出现一个可辨认的主体（人物、动物、物体或车辆）作为构图焦点。

宽泛的分类标签，区分包含明确主体的镜头和纯风景或抽象画面。

- 相关: [风景镜头](taxonomy:218) | [单一主导主体](taxonomy:222)

tutorial.en: The subject changes in the video, such as appearing, disappearing, or transitioning to another subject.

# Subject Disappearing

The video shows the main subject disappearing or leaving the frame. The subject **exits the visible area** by walking out, being obscured, or receding beyond visibility during the shot.

Subject disappearance creates **narrative tension, closure, or mystery**. A character walking out of frame can signal departure or defiance. An object fading from view can convey loss. The empty frame left behind often carries powerful emotional weight.

- Related: [Subject Revealing](taxonomy:206) | [Subject Switch](taxonomy:207)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体消失

主要主体消失或离开画面——走出画框、被遮挡或退至不可见的远处。

制造**叙事张力、结束感或悬念**。留下的空画面往往承载着强大的情感重量。

- 相关: [主体出现](taxonomy:206) | [主体切换](taxonomy:207)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Revealing

A revealing shot where the subject comes into view on screen. The subject **enters or becomes visible** during the shot, either by walking into frame, being uncovered by camera movement, or emerging from obscurity.

Revealing shots build **anticipation and surprise**. Delaying the subject's appearance creates tension; when the reveal finally occurs, it carries extra visual and narrative impact. This technique is fundamental to character introductions, plot twists, and dramatic reveals.

- Related: [Subject Disappearing](taxonomy:205) | [Subject Switch](taxonomy:207)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体出现

主体在镜头内进入视野——走入画面、被相机运动揭示或从模糊中浮现。

营造**期待感和惊喜感**，是角色介绍和剧情反转的基础手法。

- 相关: [主体消失](taxonomy:205) | [主体切换](taxonomy:207)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Switch

The main subject changes to another subject. The video's focal point **transitions from one subject to a different one** during the shot, without a cut.

Subject switching within a continuous shot demonstrates **directorial control over audience attention**. It can redirect focus during a conversation, shift from a person to an object they are looking at, or transition between characters in a complex blocking arrangement. Rack focus is one common technique for achieving subject switches.

- Related: [Subject Revealing](taxonomy:206) | [Subject Disappearing](taxonomy:205) | [Rack Focus](taxonomy:109)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体切换

画面焦点在单个连续镜头内从一个主体**过渡到另一个不同的主体**，没有剪切。

展现**导演对观众注意力的精确控制**。焦点转移是实现主体切换的常用手段。

- 相关: [主体出现](taxonomy:206) | [主体消失](taxonomy:205) | [跟焦](taxonomy:109)

tutorial.en:
# Bird's Eye

The camera maintains a bird's eye angle throughout, consistently looking straight down from above. A **bird's eye view** (or **top-down shot**) positions the camera directly overhead, perpendicular to the ground.

This extreme overhead perspective **flattens depth, transforms familiar scenes into abstract patterns, and provides an omniscient vantage point**. It can convey surveillance, divine perspective, or visual abstraction. Busby Berkeley's kaleidoscopic overhead shots of synchronized dancers in 1930s musicals remain iconic examples.

With drones, bird's eye shots have become far more common, revealing geometric patterns in cityscapes, nature, and human gatherings.

- Related: [High Angle](taxonomy:77) | [Overhead POV](taxonomy:169) | [Worm's Eye](taxonomy:80)
tutorial.zh:
# 鸟瞰

相机全程保持鸟瞰角度，从正上方垂直向下拍摄。

鸟瞰**压平纵深、将场景转化为抽象图案**，并提供全知视角。随着无人机普及，鸟瞰已成为揭示城市、自然和人群几何图案的常用手段。

- 相关: [高角度](taxonomy:77) | [俯视视角](taxonomy:169) | [虫视](taxonomy:80)

tutorial.en:
# High Angle

The camera maintains a high angle throughout, consistently looking downward compared to a level angle but not directly top-down. The camera is elevated above the subject and tilted down.

High angles make subjects appear **smaller, weaker, vulnerable, or dominated by their environment**. This psychological effect is widely used in thriller and horror films to suggest powerlessness. Conversely, high angles can provide a clear overview of spatial layouts, making them useful for **action choreography and establishing geography**.

- Related: [Bird's Eye](taxonomy:76) | [Level Angle](taxonomy:78) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 高角度

相机全程保持高角度，从上方向下看，但并非正上方垂直俯视。

高角度使主体显得**更小、更弱、更脆弱**。在惊悚片和恐怖片中广泛用于暗示无力感，同时也能提供清晰的空间布局。

- 相关: [鸟瞰](taxonomy:76) | [水平角度](taxonomy:78) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Level Angle

The camera maintains a level angle parallel to the ground (even if a Dutch angle is used) throughout the video. The lens points horizontally, matching the natural human eye line.

Level angle is the **neutral, default camera angle** that feels natural and unmanipulated. It places the viewer at the same plane as the action, creating a sense of **objectivity and equality** with the subjects. Most dialogue scenes, interviews, and everyday coverage use level angles as their baseline.

- Related: [High Angle](taxonomy:77) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 水平角度

相机全程保持与地面平行的水平角度。

**最中性的默认机位角度**，将观众置于与场景动作相同的平面上，营造客观性与平等感。

- 相关: [高角度](taxonomy:77) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Low Angle

The camera maintains a low angle throughout, consistently looking upward compared to a level angle but not directly bottom-up. The camera is positioned below the subject and tilted up.

Low angles make subjects appear **larger, more powerful, imposing, or heroic**. This is one of cinema's most effective tools for conveying dominance or authority. Orson Welles famously used extreme low angles in [*Citizen Kane* (1941)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_Kane) to emphasize Charles Foster Kane's towering ego, even building sets with ceilings to accommodate the perspective.

- Related: [Level Angle](taxonomy:78) | [Worm's Eye](taxonomy:80) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77)
tutorial.zh:
# 低角度

相机全程保持低角度，从下方向上看，但并非正下方仰视。

低角度使主体显得**更高大、更有力、更具威慑感**。威尔斯在[《公民凯恩》(1941)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_Kane)中大量使用极低角度来强调凯恩膨胀的自我。

- 相关: [水平角度](taxonomy:78) | [虫视](taxonomy:80) | [高角度](taxonomy:77)

tutorial.en:
# Worm's Eye

The camera maintains a worm's eye angle throughout, consistently looking straight up from below.

This extreme upward perspective creates maximum **distortion, grandeur, and visual drama**. Buildings tower infinitely, characters loom like giants, and ceilings become the dominant visual element. It is used sparingly for **stylized impact, surreal sequences, or to convey an insect-like or child-like ground-level perspective**.

- Related: [Low Angle](taxonomy:79) | [Bird's Eye](taxonomy:76)
tutorial.zh:
# 虫视

相机全程从正下方垂直向上拍摄。

制造最大程度的**透视扭曲和视觉冲击**——建筑无限高耸，人物如巨人般矗立。因效果极端而被谨慎使用。

- 相关: [低角度](taxonomy:79) | [鸟瞰](taxonomy:76)

tutorial.en:
# Dutch Angle

There is an obvious Dutch (canted) angle (more than 15 degrees) that occurs in the video. A **Dutch angle** (or **Dutch tilt**, **canted angle**) rotates the camera so the horizon line is no longer level, creating a diagonal composition.

The Dutch angle conveys **unease, tension, disorientation, or psychological instability**. It originated in German Expressionist cinema of the 1920s (hence "Deutsch angle") and has been used extensively in **film noir, horror, and comic book adaptations**. Tim Burton, Sam Raimi, and the cinematography of [*The Third Man* (1949)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Third_Man) are known for prominent Dutch angles.

Overuse of the Dutch angle is considered a hallmark of amateur filmmaking, so it is typically deployed deliberately for specific narrative effect.

- Related: [Dutch Angle (Varying)](taxonomy:83) | [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16)
tutorial.zh:
# 荷兰角

画面中出现明显的荷兰角（倾斜超过15度）且角度保持不变。相机旋转使地平线倾斜，形成对角线构图。

传达**不安、紧张、迷失方向或心理失衡**。起源于1920年代德国表现主义电影。

- 相关: [变化荷兰角](taxonomy:83) | [顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:14) | [逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:16)

tutorial.en: There is an obvious Dutch (canted) angle (more than 15 degrees) that occurs in the video.

# Angle Change

The camera angle changes significantly relative to the ground, moving between bird's eye, high angle, level, low angle, or worm's eye view. The **tilt orientation of the camera shifts** during the shot.

Angle changes within a single shot create **dynamic visual progression** without cutting. A shot that begins at high angle and transitions to level can shift the audience's psychological relationship with the subject from dominance to equality.

- Related: [Angle Change (High →Low)](taxonomy:63) | [Angle Change (Low →High)](taxonomy:64)
tutorial.zh:
# 角度变化

相机角度在单个连续镜头内发生显著变化，在鸟瞰、高角度、水平、低角度或虫视之间过渡。

镜头内的角度变化创造**不间断的视觉进程**。

- 相关: [角度从高到低](taxonomy:63) | [角度从低到高](taxonomy:64)

tutorial.en:
# Angle Change (High →Low)

The camera tilts up from a higher angle toward a lower one. The camera transitions from looking down to looking more level or upward.

This shift can **empower the subject over the course of the shot**, visually representing a character gaining confidence, authority, or control. It is a subtle but effective way to chart a psychological shift within continuous footage.

- Related: [Angle Change (Low →High)](taxonomy:64) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 角度从高到低

相机角度从较高角度明显上倾至较低角度。

可以在镜头进行过程中**赋予主体力量**——呈现角色获得信心或控制力的过程。

- 相关: [角度从低到高](taxonomy:64) | [高角度](taxonomy:77) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Angle Change (Low →High)

The camera tilts down from a lower angle toward a higher one. The camera transitions from looking up to looking more level or downward.

This shift can **diminish the subject's perceived power**, suggesting a loss of status, growing vulnerability, or the audience gaining an overview perspective. It reverses the empowerment arc of a high-to-low transition.

- Related: [Angle Change (High →Low)](taxonomy:63) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77)
tutorial.zh:
# 角度从低到高

相机角度从较低角度位明显下倾至较高角度。

可以**削弱主体的感知力量**，暗示地位丧失或脆弱感增长。

- 相关: [角度从高到低](taxonomy:63) | [低角度](taxonomy:79) | [高角度](taxonomy:77)

tutorial.en:
# Dutch Angle (Varying)

There is a Dutch (canted) angle that changes its degree during the video, with the horizon line not level. The **canted angle actively shifts**, becoming more or less extreme over the course of the shot.

A varying Dutch angle amplifies the sense of **instability and disorientation** beyond a static tilt. As the horizon continues to shift, the viewer's spatial anchoring is progressively undermined. This technique appears in dream sequences, intoxication scenes, and moments of extreme psychological distress.

- Related: [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:82) | [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16)
tutorial.zh:
# 变化荷兰角

画面中荷兰角的倾斜程度在持续变化，地平线始终不水平。

将**不稳定感与迷失方向感**放大到静态荷兰角无法企及的程度。常见于梦境、醉酒和心理危机场景。

- 相关: [荷兰角](taxonomy:82) | [顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:14) | [逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:16)

# Aerial Level

The camera remains at an aerial level height throughout the video. The camera is positioned **high in the air**, far above ground level, typically from a drone, helicopter, or tall crane.

Aerial-level shots provide **sweeping overviews of landscapes, cities, and large-scale events**. They establish geography, reveal patterns invisible from ground level, and create a sense of scope. In modern filmmaking, affordable drones have made aerial-level cinematography accessible to productions of all sizes.

- Related: [Overhead Level](taxonomy:132) | [Eye Level](taxonomy:129) | [Drone POV](taxonomy:165)
tutorial.zh:
# 航拍高度

相机全程处于高空，通常由无人机、直升机或大型摇臂承载。

提供**对景观、城市和大规模事件的宏观俯瞰**，建立地理环境并营造规模感。

- 相关: [架高高度](taxonomy:132) | [站立高度](taxonomy:129) | [航拍视角](taxonomy:165)

tutorial.en:
# Overhead Level

The camera is positioned at an overhead level throughout, above eye level but below aerial (around second-floor height). The camera sits **elevated but still close enough to the scene** to maintain a personal connection with subjects.

Overhead level bridges the gap between intimate eye-level and detached aerial perspectives. It is common in **sports broadcasting, event coverage, and scenes requiring a slightly elevated vantage** for clarity without losing the human scale of the action.

- Related: [Aerial Level](taxonomy:128) | [Eye Level](taxonomy:129)
tutorial.zh:
# 架高高度

相机全程处于高于站立高度但低于航拍的位置（大约二层楼高度）。

常见于**体育赛事转播、活动拍摄以及需要略高视角以获得更好清晰度的场景**。

- 相关: [航拍高度](taxonomy:128) | [站立高度](taxonomy:129)

tutorial.en:
# Eye Level

The camera is positioned at eye level throughout (roughly at a person's eye height, above the waist). The lens sits at approximately **5 to 6 feet from the ground**, matching the natural human standing perspective.

Eye level is the **default, neutral camera height** that feels most natural and unmanipulated to viewers. It creates a sense of being present in the scene as a human observer. Most dialogue scenes, documentaries, and everyday coverage use eye-level placement.

- Related: [Overhead Level](taxonomy:132) | [Hip Level](taxonomy:131)
tutorial.zh:
# 站立高度

相机全程处于人眼站立高度（距地面约1.5至1.8米）。

**最中性的默认机位高度**，给观众最自然的在场感。

- 相关: [架高高度](taxonomy:132) | [低机位](taxonomy:131)

tutorial.en:
# Hip Level

The camera is positioned at hip level throughout, roughly between knee and waist height, whether or not a human subject is present. The lens sits at approximately **2 to 3.5 feet from the ground**.

Hip-level shots create a **subtly different perspective from eye level**, often used in Westerns (the classic "cowboy shot" height), children's-eye-view scenes, and any scenario where a slightly low vantage adds visual interest. It can make environments feel taller and more imposing.

- Related: [Eye Level](taxonomy:129) | [Ground Level](taxonomy:130)
tutorial.zh:
# 低机位

相机全程处于膝盖到腰部之间的高度。

制造与平视**微妙不同的视角**，常用于西部片（牛仔镜头高度）和儿童视角场景。

- 相关: [站立高度](taxonomy:129) | [贴地](taxonomy:130)

tutorial.en:
# Ground Level

The camera is positioned at ground level throughout, close to the ground. The lens sits **at or very near floor or ground surface**, looking across the ground plane.

Ground-level shots create a **dramatic, worm's-eye-adjacent perspective** that makes everything above the camera appear towering. They are used for **revealing footsteps, showing characters' shoes, capturing insects or small animals, and creating a sense of vulnerability or smallness**. Kubrick used ground-level tracking in [*A Clockwork Orange* (1971)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Clockwork_Orange_(film)) for unsettling effect.

- Related: [Hip Level](taxonomy:131) | [Worm's Eye](taxonomy:80)
tutorial.zh:
# 贴地

相机全程紧贴地面。

制造**戏剧性的极低视角**——相机上方一切都显得高耸。用于展示脚步、小动物或营造渺小感。

- 相关: [低机位](taxonomy:131) | [虫视](taxonomy:80)

tutorial.en:
# Ground Height Change (High →Low)

The camera height decreases noticeably in relation to the ground, shifting between levels like aerial, overhead, eye, hip, or ground. The camera **descends from a higher to a lower position** during the shot.

Descending height shifts can **bring the camera closer to the action, transition from establishing overview to intimate ground level, or create a sense of descending into a situation**.

- Related: [Ground Height Change (Low →High)](taxonomy:127) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
# 地面高度从高到低

相机高度在镜头内明显降低。

可以**将相机带入更接近动作的位置**，从全景概览过渡到地面视角。

- 相关: [地面高度从低到高](taxonomy:127) | [降](taxonomy:32) | [摇臂降](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Ground Height Change (Low →High)

The camera height increases noticeably in relation to the ground, shifting between levels like aerial, overhead, eye, hip, or ground. The camera **rises from a lower to a higher position** during the shot.

Ascending height shifts can **reveal broader context, create a sense of liberation or escape, or transition from an intimate detail to an establishing overview**.

- Related: [Ground Height Change (High →Low)](taxonomy:126) | [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Crane Up](taxonomy:4)
tutorial.zh:
# 地面高度从低到高

相机高度在镜头内明显升高。

可以**揭示更广阔的环境、营造解放感或从细节过渡到全景概览**。

- 相关: [地面高度从高到低](taxonomy:126) | [升](taxonomy:38) | [摇臂升](taxonomy:4)

# Underwater Level

The camera is fully submerged underwater throughout the video. The entire frame shows the **underwater environment**, with visual characteristics like refracted light, suspended particles, and the distinctive blue-green color palette of subaquatic filming.

Underwater cinematography creates an **alien, immersive visual world** with unique lighting physics. It is essential in nature documentaries, swimming sequences, and fantasy or sci-fi films depicting submerged environments. Pioneering underwater cinematographer [Jack Cardiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Cardiff) helped establish techniques still used today.

- Related: [Water Level](taxonomy:134) | [Above Water →Underwater](taxonomy:118)
tutorial.zh:
# 水下

相机全程完全沉浸在水中，画面展示水下环境。

水下摄影创造**独特的沉浸式视觉空间**，在自然纪录片和水下场景中不可或缺。

- 相关: [水面](taxonomy:134) | [从水上到水下](taxonomy:118)

tutorial.en:
# Water Level

The camera is positioned at water level throughout. The camera is situated above the water surface yet below aerial height, maintaining a low-altitude perspective between the waterline and the airspace.

Water-level shots are used in **surfing films, naval scenes, swimming sequences, and nature documentaries** showing animals at the water's edge. The technique places the viewer above the surface tension, creating visceral proximity to the water.

- Related: [Underwater Level](taxonomy:133) | [Above Water →Underwater](taxonomy:118)
tutorial.zh:
# 水面

相机全程位于水面之上，但低于航拍高度的位置。

- 相关: [水下](taxonomy:133) | [从水上到水下](taxonomy:118)

tutorial.en:
# Above Water →Underwater

The camera transitions from above water to underwater. The shot begins above the surface and **plunges beneath**, revealing the underwater world in a single continuous take.

This transition is a **dramatic visual reveal** that transports the audience from one environment to another. It is used in diving sequences, nature documentaries showing marine life, and stylized transitions. The moment of crossing the waterline creates a striking visual boundary.

- Related: [Underwater →Above Water](taxonomy:142) | [Underwater Level](taxonomy:133)
tutorial.zh:
# 从水上到水下

相机在单个连续镜头中从水面上方潜入水下。

穿越水面的瞬间制造**戏剧性的环境分界**。

- 相关: [从水下到水上](taxonomy:142) | [水下](taxonomy:133)

tutorial.en:
# Underwater →Above Water

The camera transitions from underwater to above water. The shot begins submerged and **rises to break the surface**, revealing the above-water world.

This transition can convey **emergence, surfacing, gasping for air, or revelation**. The visual shift from the distorted, blue-tinted underwater world to the clarity and brightness above creates a powerful sensory contrast. It often symbolizes rebirth, escape, or awakening.

- Related: [Above Water →Underwater](taxonomy:118) | [Water Level](taxonomy:134)
tutorial.zh:
# 从水下到水上

相机在单个连续镜头中从水下浮出水面。

从水下到水面的视觉反差传达**浮出、喘息或觉醒**的感觉。

- 相关: [从水上到水下](taxonomy:118) | [水面](taxonomy:134)

tutorial.en:
# Above Subject

The camera remains positioned above the subject throughout the video. The camera is consistently placed **higher than the subject**, looking down at them.

This positioning conveys the subject's **vulnerability, subordination, or smallness** relative to the camera (and by extension, the viewer). It is the height equivalent of a high angle, though height and angle are independent: a camera can be above the subject while pointed level.

- Related: [At Subject](taxonomy:156) | [Below Subject](taxonomy:157) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77)
tutorial.zh:
# 高于主体

相机全程位于主体上方。

传达主体的**脆弱感、从属感或渺小感**。

- 相关: [与主体等高](taxonomy:156) | [低于主体](taxonomy:157) | [高角度](taxonomy:77)

tutorial.en:
# At Subject

The camera remains positioned at about the same height as the subject throughout the video. The camera is at **eye level with the subject**, creating a sense of equality and direct engagement.

Eye-level subject framing is the **most neutral and natural** camera-subject relationship. It implies neither dominance nor submission, making it the default for dialogue, interviews, and objective coverage.

- Related: [Above Subject](taxonomy:155) | [Below Subject](taxonomy:157) | [Eye Level](taxonomy:129)
tutorial.zh:
# 与主体等高

相机全程与主体大致等高。

**最中性、最自然**的相机与主体关系，是对话和采访的默认选择。

- 相关: [高于主体](taxonomy:155) | [低于主体](taxonomy:157) | [站立高度](taxonomy:129)

tutorial.en:
# Below Subject

The camera remains positioned below the subject throughout the video. The camera is consistently placed **lower than the subject**, looking up at them.

Shooting from below a subject conveys **power, authority, heroism, or menace**. It is the height equivalent of a low angle and is used to make characters feel dominant or imposing. Combined with a low angle, it creates the strongest sense of looking up at a powerful figure.

- Related: [At Subject](taxonomy:156) | [Above Subject](taxonomy:155) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 低于主体

相机全程位于主体下方。

传达主体的**力量感、权威感或威胁感**。

- 相关: [与主体等高](taxonomy:156) | [高于主体](taxonomy:155) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Height Change

The camera's height relative to the subject (above, at level, or below) is different at the end compared to the beginning. The **camera-to-subject vertical relationship shifts** during the shot.

Subject height changes within a continuous shot can **chart a psychological arc** as the subject gains or loses power, or as the camera deliberately repositions to alter the audience's relationship with the character.

- Related: [Subject Height Change (High →Low)](taxonomy:153) | [Subject Height Change (Low →High)](taxonomy:154)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体相对高度变化

相机与主体的高度关系在镜头内发生变化。

可以**描绘心理弧线**——伴随主体力量的获得或丧失而变化。

- 相关: [主体相对高度从高到低](taxonomy:153) | [主体相对高度从低到高](taxonomy:154)

display_name.zh: 主体相对高度从高到低

tutorial.en:
# Subject Height Change (High →Low)

The subject starts above and ends at or below the camera's height, or starts level and ends below. The camera's position **descends relative to the subject** (or the subject rises relative to the camera).

This transition can convey the subject **gaining power or stature** over the course of the shot, as the audience's vantage shifts from looking down to looking up.

- Related: [Subject Height Change (Low →High)](taxonomy:154) | [Above Subject](taxonomy:155) | [Below Subject](taxonomy:157)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体相对高度从高到低

相机从主体上方过渡到等高或低于主体的位置。

传达主体**获得力量或地位**的过程。

- 相关: [主体相对高度从低到高](taxonomy:154)

display_name.zh: 主体相对高度从低到高

tutorial.en:
# Subject Height Change (Low →High)

The subject starts below and ends at or above the camera's height, or starts level and ends above. The camera's position **ascends relative to the subject** (or the subject descends relative to the camera).

This transition can convey the subject **losing power or becoming diminished**, as the audience's vantage shifts from looking up to looking down.

- Related: [Subject Height Change (High →Low)](taxonomy:153) | [Below Subject](taxonomy:157) | [Above Subject](taxonomy:155)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体相对高度从低到高

相机从主体下方过渡到等高或高于主体的位置。

传达主体**失去力量或变得渺小**的过程。

- 相关: [主体相对高度从高到低](taxonomy:153)

# First-Person POV

A first-person POV shot, filmed as if seen directly through the character's eyes. The camera represents **exactly what the character sees**, with the character's body not visible (or only hands/limbs at the frame edges).

First-person POV creates **maximum subjective immersion**, placing the viewer inside the character's head. It is used in horror films for suspense ([*Halloween* (1978)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halloween_(1978))), action sequences for visceral impact, and VR content. Full first-person films like [*Hardcore Henry* (2015)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_Henry) push the technique to its extreme.

- Related: [Selfie POV](taxonomy:171) | [Locked-On POV](taxonomy:167)
tutorial.zh:
# 第一人称视角

画面呈现角色眼中所见的精确画面，角色本身不可见。

创造**最强的主观沉浸感**。在恐怖片中用于制造悬疑，在动作片中增强临场感。

- 相关: [自拍视角](taxonomy:171) | [固定机位视角](taxonomy:167)

tutorial.en:
# Broadcast POV

The video shows a broadcast-style viewpoint used in television production. The camera adopts the **conventions of live TV broadcasting**, including fixed multi-camera setups, switcher-style cuts, and standardized framing for news, sports, talk shows, or event coverage.

Broadcast POV prioritizes **clarity, consistency, and coverage** over cinematic artistry. Cameras are typically positioned at predetermined stations to ensure reliable sight lines and quick switching between angles.

- Related: [Objective POV](taxonomy:168)
tutorial.zh:
# 转播视角

采用电视直播的拍摄惯例——固定多机位、切换台式镜头切换和标准化构图。

优先考虑**清晰度、一致性和覆盖面**而非电影化的艺术感。

- 相关: [客观视角](taxonomy:168)

tutorial.en:
# Dashcam POV

A forward-facing dashcam view from a vehicle-mounted camera, capturing the scene ahead. The camera is **fixed to the vehicle's dashboard or windshield**, providing a continuous first-person view of the road.

Dashcam footage has a distinctive look: **wide-angle, slightly distorted, with the hood or dashboard visible** at the bottom of frame. Originally utilitarian (insurance documentation, police body cameras), the dashcam aesthetic has been adopted by filmmakers for **raw, immediate driving sequences** and has become its own genre of online video.

- Related: [First-Person POV](taxonomy:166) | [Locked-On POV](taxonomy:167)
tutorial.zh:
# 行车记录仪视角

安装在车辆仪表板或挡风玻璃上的前向固定相机，持续拍摄前方道路。

画面特征为**广角、略有畸变，底部可见引擎盖**。

- 相关: [第一人称视角](taxonomy:166) | [固定机位视角](taxonomy:167)

tutorial.en:
# Drone POV

A drone POV showing an aerial view. The camera is mounted on an **unmanned aerial vehicle**, providing elevated perspectives ranging from just above head height to hundreds of feet in the air.

Drone POV has transformed modern cinematography since the mid-2010s, **democratizing aerial shots** that previously required expensive helicopter rigs. Drones enable smooth aerial tracking, orbits, reveals, and top-down compositions. Their distinctive look includes gentle floating motion and wide-angle perspectives from unusual heights.

- Related: [Aerial Level](taxonomy:128) | [Aerial Tracking Shot](taxonomy:41)
tutorial.zh:
# 航拍视角

相机安装在无人机或飞行器上，提供较高的空中视角。

- 相关: [航拍高度](taxonomy:128) | [航拍跟踪](taxonomy:41)

tutorial.en:
# Locked-On POV

A locked-on POV shot where the camera is mounted to an object, keeping its perspective fixed with that object. The camera is **physically attached to a vehicle, weapon, tool, or other object**, and the frame moves exactly as the object moves.

Locked-on shots create a **visceral, mechanical perspective** that ties the viewer to the object's motion. Examples include cameras mounted on car bumpers, skateboard decks, spinning wheels, or the barrels of guns. The technique emphasizes speed, rotation, or impact from the object's own viewpoint.

- Related: [Dashcam POV](taxonomy:164) | [First-Person POV](taxonomy:166)
tutorial.zh:
# 固定机位视角

相机物理安装在某个物体上（车辆、武器、工具等），视角与该物体保持锁定。

制造**身临其境的机械视角**，强调速度感、旋转感或冲击力。

- 相关: [行车记录仪视角](taxonomy:164) | [第一人称视角](taxonomy:166)

tutorial.en:
# Objective POV

An objective POV shot where the camera captures the scene from a detached, observational perspective. The camera does **not represent any character's viewpoint** but instead observes the scene as a neutral, invisible witness.

Objective POV is the **default mode of most narrative filmmaking**: the camera shows the action from angles no character occupies, maintaining an omniscient or reportorial stance. It allows filmmakers to compose for visual impact and storytelling clarity without being constrained by any character's physical position.

- Related: [First-Person POV](taxonomy:166) | [Broadcast POV](taxonomy:163)
tutorial.zh:
# 客观视角

相机从超然的观察者角度拍摄，不代表任何角色的视点。

**大多数叙事电影的默认模式**，允许为视觉冲击力和叙事清晰度自由构图。

- 相关: [第一人称视角](taxonomy:166) | [转播视角](taxonomy:163)

tutorial.en:
# Overhead POV

An overhead POV shot where the camera is positioned directly above the subject for a top-down perspective. The camera looks **straight down at the subject**, creating a flat, map-like view.

Overhead POV is used for **cooking shows, craft demonstrations, surgical footage, and artistic compositions** where the top-down view reveals spatial relationships invisible from other angles. In narrative film, it can represent a deity's perspective, surveillance, or abstract visual design.

- Related: [Bird's Eye](taxonomy:76) | [Aerial Level](taxonomy:128)
tutorial.zh:
# 顶视视角

相机位于主体正上方进行自上而下的拍摄。

用于**烹饪节目、手工教程、外科手术画面和艺术构图**等需要顶视角的场景。

- 相关: [鸟瞰](taxonomy:76) | [航拍高度](taxonomy:128)

tutorial.en:
# Screen Recording POV

A screen recording of a software or system interface (e.g., menus, windows, toolbars). The video captures **what appears on a computer, phone, or device screen**, showing digital interfaces rather than physical-world footage.

Screen recording POV has become increasingly common in **tutorials, tech reviews, gaming streams, and "screenlife" films** like [*Searching* (2018)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Searching_(film)) and [*Unfriended* (2014)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unfriended), where the entire narrative unfolds through screens and interfaces.

- Related: [Broadcast POV](taxonomy:163)
tutorial.zh:
# 屏幕录制视角

捕捉电脑、手机或设备屏幕上的显示内容。

在**教程、科技评测、游戏直播和「屏幕叙事」电影**中日益普遍。

- 相关: [转播视角](taxonomy:163)

tutorial.en:
# Selfie POV

A selfie POV shot where the camera is held by the person being filmed (e.g., by hand, selfie stick, or invisible selfie rod) and faces them. The camera is at **arm's length or selfie-stick distance**, showing the subject's face with a slightly wide-angle, close-up perspective.

Selfie POV has become one of the most recognizable visual idioms of the smartphone era. In filmmaking, it conveys **self-documentation, vlogging, social media culture, or a character's desire to record themselves**. The distinctive wide-angle distortion and visible arm or stick are part of the aesthetic.

- Related: [First-Person POV](taxonomy:166)
tutorial.zh:
# 自拍视角

相机由被拍摄者自己手持（手、自拍杆等）并对准自己。

智能手机时代最具辨识度的视觉语汇之一，传达**自我记录和社交媒体文化**。

- 相关: [第一人称视角](taxonomy:166)

tutorial.en:
# Third-Person Full-Body Game POV

A third-person 3D game video where the entire character is visible on screen. The camera is positioned **behind and above the player character**, showing their full body within the game environment.

This is the standard camera for action-adventure and open-world games. It provides **spatial awareness while maintaining character identity**, letting the player see both their avatar and the surrounding environment.

- Related: [Third-Person Over-the-Shoulder POV](taxonomy:175) | [Third-Person Over-the-Hip POV](taxonomy:174)
tutorial.zh:
# 全身游戏视角

第三人称3D游戏视频，角色全身在屏幕上可见。相机位于玩家角色后上方。

动作冒险和开放世界游戏的标准视角，在**保持角色身份认同的同时提供空间感知**。

- 相关: [过肩视角](taxonomy:175) | [过臀视角](taxonomy:174)

tutorial.en:
# Third-Person Isometric Game POV

A third-person isometric (2.5D) gaming video with a tilted overhead angle showing both the top and side planes of the environment in a three-quarters perspective, with minimal perspective distortion.

Isometric views are a staple of **strategy games, RPGs, and simulation games** (e.g., *Diablo*, *SimCity*, *Baldur's Gate*). The fixed elevated angle provides **clear spatial overview** while maintaining a sense of three-dimensionality without true perspective foreshortening.

- Related: [Third-Person Top-Down Game POV](taxonomy:177) | [Third-Person Side View Game POV](taxonomy:176)
tutorial.zh:
# 等距游戏视角

等距（2.5D）游戏视频，以四分之三透视展示环境的顶面和侧面。

**策略游戏、RPG和模拟经营类游戏**的核心视角，提供清晰的空间概览。

- 相关: [俯视游戏视角](taxonomy:177) | [侧视游戏视角](taxonomy:176)

tutorial.en:
# Third-Person Over-the-Hip POV

A third-person over-the-hip POV shot framing the character from the hip up. The camera is positioned **behind the character at hip level**, showing from approximately the waist upward.

This framing is common in **third-person shooters and action games** where the wider view provides better spatial awareness for combat while keeping the character's upper body and weapon visible.

- Related: [Third-Person Over-the-Shoulder POV](taxonomy:175) | [Third-Person Full-Body Game POV](taxonomy:172)
tutorial.zh:
# 过臀视角

相机位于角色身后臀部高度，展示腰部以上。

在**第三人称射击和动作游戏**中常见，较宽的视野利于战斗中的空间感知。

- 相关: [过肩视角](taxonomy:175) | [全身游戏视角](taxonomy:172)

tutorial.en:
# Third-Person Over-the-Shoulder POV

An over-the-shoulder POV where the camera is positioned behind the character, showing their upper body and the scene ahead. The camera sits **just behind and to one side of the character's shoulder**.

This is the dominant camera in modern third-person action games (e.g., [*The Last of Us*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_Us), *God of War*). It provides **tight, cinematic framing** that creates immersion while maintaining spatial awareness. In film, the over-the-shoulder angle is a staple of dialogue coverage.

- Related: [Third-Person Over-the-Hip POV](taxonomy:174) | [Third-Person Full-Body Game POV](taxonomy:172)
tutorial.zh:
# 过肩视角

相机位于角色肩膀后方偏侧，展示上半身和前方场景。

现代第三人称动作游戏的主流视角，提供**紧凑的电影化构图**。在电影中是对话覆盖的经典手法。

- 相关: [过臀视角](taxonomy:174) | [全身游戏视角](taxonomy:172)

tutorial.en:
# Third-Person Side View Game POV

A side-view gaming video where the camera is placed to the side, capturing the scene or character in profile. The action unfolds on a **2D plane viewed from the side**.

Side-view perspective is the foundation of **platformers, fighting games, and classic side-scrolling genres** (e.g., *Super Mario Bros.*, *Street Fighter*). It provides clear spatial orientation for horizontal movement and jumping mechanics.

- Related: [Third-Person Isometric Game POV](taxonomy:173) | [Third-Person Top-Down Game POV](taxonomy:177)
tutorial.zh:
# 侧视游戏视角

侧视游戏视频，动作在从侧面观看的2D平面上展开。

**平台跳跃游戏和格斗游戏**的基础视角。

- 相关: [等距游戏视角](taxonomy:173) | [俯视游戏视角](taxonomy:177)

tutorial.en:
# Third-Person Top-Down Game POV

A gaming video with a top-down or oblique top-down view, where the camera is placed above the character and environment, looking downward to show mostly the tops of objects with limited sides.

Top-down perspective is used in **twin-stick shooters, strategy games, and retro-styled games**. It provides a **clear tactical overview** of the playfield, emphasizing spatial positioning over character detail.

- Related: [Third-Person Isometric Game POV](taxonomy:173) | [Bird's Eye](taxonomy:76)
tutorial.zh:
# 俯视游戏视角

俯视或斜俯视游戏视频，以物体顶面为主展示。

**双摇杆射击和策略游戏**的核心视角，提供清晰的战术概览。

- 相关: [等距游戏视角](taxonomy:173) | [鸟瞰](taxonomy:76)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly

The camera dollies (translates forward or backward) relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **dolly** physically moves the camera closer to or farther from the scene, changing perspective through real spatial displacement.

Dolly movement is distinct from zooming: it introduces parallax (foreground objects shift relative to background), creating a natural depth effect that zooms cannot replicate. This makes dollying the preferred technique for **intimate character moments, dramatic reveals, and immersive forward progression**.

- Related: [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Zoom](taxonomy:21)
tutorial.zh:
# 推拉

相机相对地面进行前后推拉，可能同时伴随其他运动。**推拉**通过物理位移改变透视关系。

推拉引入视差——前景物体相对背景发生位移——创造出变焦无法复制的自然深度效果。是**亲密角色时刻和戏剧性揭示**的首选技法。

- 相关: [推](taxonomy:35) | [拉](taxonomy:29) | [变焦](taxonomy:21)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Forward

The camera only moves physically forward (not zoom in) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **dolly in** pushes the camera closer to the subject, compressing the apparent distance between foreground and background through natural parallax.

Unlike a [Zoom In](taxonomy:22), which magnifies without moving the camera, a dolly forward changes perspective: foreground objects grow faster than background objects, drawing the viewer into the scene. This depth-driven immersion is why dollying is often preferred over zooming for dramatic moments.

The dolly dates to the silent era; D.W. Griffith is often credited with early dolly experiments. The invention of the Western Dolly in the 1930s and the Steadicam in 1975 vastly expanded how filmmakers could execute forward movement.

- Related: [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25)
tutorial.zh:
# 推

相机仅相对地面向前物理移动（非变焦推入），没有其他运动。

**推**使相机靠近主体，通过视差压缩前景与背景的距离感，将观众拉入场景。是叙事电影中最常用的运镜之一。

- 相关: [拉](taxonomy:29) | [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Backward

The camera only moves physically backward (not zoom out) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **dolly out** pulls the camera away from the subject, expanding the visible environment and revealing the broader context around the subject.

Filmmakers use dolly backward to **create emotional distance, reveal isolation, or widen from an intimate moment to a larger scene**. A slow dolly out at the end of a scene is a classic way to signal closure or reflection.

- Related: [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 拉

相机仅相对地面向后物理移动（非变焦拉远），没有其他运动。

**拉**使相机远离主体，扩展可见环境。常用于**营造情感距离、揭示孤立感或从亲密时刻扩展到宏大场景**。

- 相关: [推](taxonomy:35) | [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Has Dolly

The camera dollies (translates forward or backward) relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_translation classifiers) to identify any forward or backward displacement.

- Related: [Has Dolly Forward](taxonomy:311) | [Has Dolly Backward](taxonomy:27)
tutorial.zh:
# 含推拉

相机相对地面进行前后推拉，可能同时伴随其他运动。使用**存在性检测**识别任何前后位移。

- 相关: [含推](taxonomy:311) | [含拉](taxonomy:27)

tutorial.en:
# Has Dolly Forward Movement (Incl. Extreme Angles)

The camera moves forward relative to the scene, including bird's-eye and worm's-eye views where ground-relative forward maps to north/south respectively. This is a **broader variant** of the standard forward dolly label that accounts for extreme viewing angles.

- Related: [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Has Dolly Movement](taxonomy:33)
tutorial.zh:
# 含推（含极端角度）

相机相对场景向前运动，将鸟瞰和虫视角度下的等效运动纳入考量。

标准推标签的**广义变体**。

- 相关: [推](taxonomy:35) | [含推拉](taxonomy:310)

tutorial.en:
# Has Dolly Backward Movement (Incl. Extreme Angles)

The camera moves backward relative to the scene, including bird's-eye and worm's-eye views where ground-relative backward maps to south/north respectively. This is a **broader variant** of the standard backward dolly label that accounts for extreme viewing angles.

- Related: [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Has Dolly Movement](taxonomy:33)
tutorial.zh:
# 含拉（含极端角度）

相机相对场景向后运动，将鸟瞰和虫视角度下的等效运动纳入考量。

标准拉标签的**广义变体**。

- 相关: [拉](taxonomy:29) | [含推拉](taxonomy:310)

tutorial.en:
# Has Dolly Forward

The camera moves physically forward relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any forward translation** regardless of whether other movements are present.

- Related: [Has Dolly Backward](taxonomy:27) | [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35)
tutorial.zh:
# 含推

相机相对地面向前物理位移，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含拉](taxonomy:27) | [推](taxonomy:35)

tutorial.en:
# Has Backward Movement (Relative to Ground)

The camera moves physically backward relative to the ground at some point during the shot, potentially combined with other movements. This label detects **any backward dolly component** in the camera's motion, excluding bird's-eye and worm's-eye views where "forward" and "backward" are ambiguous.

- Related: [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Has Dolly Movement](taxonomy:33)
tutorial.zh:
# 含拉

相机相对地面向后物理位移，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含推](taxonomy:311) | [拉](taxonomy:29)

tutorial.en:
# Truck

The camera trucks (translates laterally) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **truck** physically displaces the camera left or right, producing parallax between foreground and background elements.

Trucking creates a more immersive, three-dimensional feel than panning because the physical displacement reveals depth relationships in the scene. It is essential for **tracking lateral movement, creating flowing compositions, and building spatial awareness**.

- Related: [Truck Left](taxonomy:6) | [Truck Right](taxonomy:12) | [Pan](taxonomy:7)
tutorial.zh:
# 横移

相机进行横向平移，可能同时伴随其他运动。**横移**使相机整体向左或向右物理位移，产生视差。

横移比摇镜更具沉浸感和立体感，因为物理位移揭示了场景的深度关系。

- 相关: [横移左](taxonomy:6) | [横移右](taxonomy:12) | [摇镜](taxonomy:7)

tutorial.en:
# Truck Left

The camera only moves physically leftward without any other camera movement. A **truck** (also called a **tracking shot** or **crab**) translates the entire camera body sideways along a horizontal axis. Unlike a [Pan Left](taxonomy:8), which merely pivots, a truck physically displaces the camera, producing parallax between foreground and background objects.

Filmmakers use truck left to **follow a subject walking screen-left, reveal depth in a scene, or create a flowing lateral composition**. Because trucking introduces real parallax, it feels more immersive and three-dimensional than a pan.

Historically, truck shots required dolly tracks or wheeled platforms. Modern stabilizers (Steadicam, gimbals) and drones have made smooth lateral movement far more accessible.

- Related: [Truck Right](taxonomy:12) | [Pan Left](taxonomy:8)
tutorial.zh:
# 横移左

相机仅向左进行物理横移，没有其他运动。与[左摇镜](taxonomy:8)不同，横移涉及相机的物理位移，产生视差。

用于**跟随向左移动的主体、展示场景深度或创造流畅的横向构图**。

- 相关: [横移右](taxonomy:12) | [左摇镜](taxonomy:8)

tutorial.en:
# Truck Right

The camera only moves physically rightward without any other camera movement. A **truck right** translates the camera body to the right, creating parallax between foreground and background elements. Unlike a [Pan Right](taxonomy:10), the camera physically moves rather than pivoting.

Truck right shares the same cinematic applications as truck left: **following lateral subject movement, revealing spatial depth, and composing dynamic lateral shots**. The direction is chosen to match the subject's motion or the desired reveal direction.

- Related: [Truck Left](taxonomy:6) | [Pan Right](taxonomy:10)
tutorial.zh:
# 横移右

相机仅向右进行物理横移，没有其他运动。与[右摇镜](taxonomy:10)不同，横移涉及相机的物理位移，产生视差。

用于**跟随向右移动的主体或创造与画面内运动匹配的横向构图**。

- 相关: [横移左](taxonomy:6) | [右摇镜](taxonomy:10)

tutorial.en:
# Has Truck

The camera trucks (translates laterally) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_translation classifiers) to identify any lateral displacement.

- Related: [Has Truck Left](taxonomy:309) | [Has Truck Right](taxonomy:11)
tutorial.zh:
# 含横移

相机进行横向平移，可能同时伴随其他运动。使用**存在性检测**识别任何横向位移。

- 相关: [含左移](taxonomy:309) | [含右移](taxonomy:11)

tutorial.en:
# Has Truck Left

The camera moves physically leftward, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any leftward lateral translation** regardless of whether other movements are present.

- Related: [Has Truck Right](taxonomy:11) | [Truck Left](taxonomy:6)
tutorial.zh:
# 含左移

相机向左物理横移，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含右移](taxonomy:11) | [横移左](taxonomy:6)

tutorial.en:
# Has Rightward Movement

The camera moves physically rightward at some point during the shot, potentially combined with other movements. This label detects **any rightward truck component** in the camera's motion.

- Related: [Truck Right](taxonomy:12) | [Has Truck Movement](taxonomy:5)
tutorial.zh:
# 含右移

相机向右物理横移，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含左移](taxonomy:309) | [横移右](taxonomy:12)

tutorial.en:
# Pedestal

The camera pedestals (translates vertically) relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **pedestal** physically raises or lowers the camera while maintaining its angle, unlike a tilt which pivots in place.

Pedestal movement creates a clean vertical shift in vantage point, used to **follow rising or descending subjects, adjust camera height for different shot sizes, or create smooth vertical reveals** without the angular change of a tilt or the arcing path of a crane.

- Related: [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Tilt](taxonomy:19)
tutorial.zh:
# 升降

相机相对地面进行垂直升降，可能同时伴随其他运动。**升降**在保持角度不变的情况下物理升高或降低相机。

产生纯粹的垂直视角变化，不带有俯仰的角度变化或摇臂的弧形路径。

- 相关: [升](taxonomy:38) | [降](taxonomy:32) | [俯仰](taxonomy:19)

tutorial.en:
# Pedestal Up

The camera only moves physically upward (not tilt up) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **pedestal up** (or **boom up**) raises the camera vertically while maintaining its angle, unlike a [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) which pivots in place, or a [Crane Up](taxonomy:4) which arcs along a curved path.

Filmmakers pedestal up to **follow a rising subject, gradually reveal overhead elements, or shift the camera's vantage point from a low angle to a higher perspective**. The movement maintains a constant viewing angle to the ground, producing a clean vertical translation without the perspective rotation of a tilt.

- Related: [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Crane Up](taxonomy:4)
tutorial.zh:
# 升

相机仅相对地面向上物理移动（非上仰），没有其他运动。与[上仰](taxonomy:20)或[垂直弧形升](taxonomy:4)不同。

用于**跟随上升的主体或调整机位高度**，同时保持地平线稳定。

- 相关: [降](taxonomy:32) | [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [垂直弧形升](taxonomy:4)

tutorial.en:
# Pedestal Down

The camera only moves physically downward (not tilt down) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **pedestal down** (or **boom down**) lowers the camera vertically while maintaining its angle, unlike a [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) or [Crane Down](taxonomy:3).

Filmmakers pedestal down to **follow a descending subject, lower the camera to a child's or pet's eye level, or shift from an elevated vantage to ground level**. The movement preserves the camera's angular orientation, keeping horizon lines steady.

- Related: [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
# 降

相机仅相对地面向下物理移动（非下俯），没有其他运动。与[下俯](taxonomy:18)或[垂直弧形降](taxonomy:3)不同。

用于**跟随下降的主体或将机位降至更低的视角**。

- 相关: [升](taxonomy:38) | [下俯](taxonomy:18) | [垂直弧形降](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pedestal

The camera pedestals (translates vertically) relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_translation classifiers) to identify any vertical displacement.

- Related: [Has Pedestal Up](taxonomy:313) | [Has Pedestal Down](taxonomy:30)
tutorial.zh:
# 含升降

相机相对地面进行垂直升降，可能同时伴随其他运动。使用**存在性检测**识别任何垂直位移。

- 相关: [含升](taxonomy:313) | [含降](taxonomy:30)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pedestal Up Movement (Incl. Extreme Angles)

The camera moves physically upward relative to the ground, including bird's-eye and worm's-eye views. This is a **broader variant** that accounts for extreme viewing angles where the ground-relative vertical direction is still meaningful.

- Related: [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Has Pedestal Movement](taxonomy:36)
tutorial.zh:
# 含升（含极端角度）

相机相对地面向上运动，将极端拍摄角度纳入考量。

标准升标签的**广义变体**。

- 相关: [升](taxonomy:38) | [含升降](taxonomy:312)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pedestal Down Movement (Incl. Extreme Angles)

The camera moves physically downward relative to the ground, including bird's-eye and worm's-eye views. This is a **broader variant** that accounts for extreme viewing angles.

- Related: [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Has Pedestal Movement](taxonomy:36)
tutorial.zh:
# 含降（含极端角度）

相机相对地面向下运动，将极端拍摄角度纳入考量。

标准降标签的**广义变体**。

- 相关: [降](taxonomy:32) | [含升降](taxonomy:312)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pedestal Up

The camera moves physically upward relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any upward vertical translation** regardless of whether other movements are present.

- Related: [Has Pedestal Down](taxonomy:30) | [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38)
tutorial.zh:
# 含升

相机相对地面向上物理位移，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含降](taxonomy:30) | [升](taxonomy:38)

tutorial.en:
# Has Downward Movement (Relative to Ground)

The camera moves physically downward relative to the ground at some point during the shot, potentially combined with other movements. This label detects **any downward pedestal component**, excluding bird's-eye and worm's-eye views.

- Related: [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Has Pedestal Movement](taxonomy:36)
tutorial.zh:
# 含降

相机相对地面向下物理位移，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含升](taxonomy:313) | [降](taxonomy:32)

tutorial.en:
# Roll

The camera rolls (rotates around the optical axis) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **roll** tilts the horizon line by rotating the entire frame clockwise or counterclockwise.

Roll is among the most disorienting camera movements and is used sparingly for **dream sequences, psychological disturbance, point-of-view shots from a tumbling character, or stylized transitions**.

- Related: [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16) | [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:82)
tutorial.zh:
# 翻滚

相机绕光轴旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。**翻滚**使地平线倾斜。

因直接打破观众的空间定向感而被谨慎使用，传达**梦境、心理失衡或风格化转场**。

- 相关: [顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:14) | [逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:16) | [荷兰角](taxonomy:82)

tutorial.en:
# Roll Clockwise

The camera only rolls clockwise without any other camera movement. A **roll** rotates the camera around its optical axis (the line from lens to subject), tilting the horizon line. Clockwise roll causes the frame's horizon to rotate so the left side rises and the right side dips.

Roll is used sparingly because it breaks the audience's sense of spatial orientation. Filmmakers employ it to **convey disorientation, dream states, or a character's altered perception**. A sustained roll can suggest the world turning upside down, while a quick snap-roll can punctuate a moment of shock.

The Dutch angle (or canted angle) is a related but distinct concept: it is a static tilt of the frame, whereas a roll is a continuous rotation. Some filmmakers transition from a Dutch angle into a roll to intensify unease.

- Related: [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16) | [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:83)
tutorial.zh:
# 顺时针翻滚

相机仅绕光轴顺时针旋转，没有其他运动。画面左侧上升、右侧下降。

传达**迷失方向感、梦境状态或角色感知的改变**。

- 相关: [逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:16) | [荷兰角](taxonomy:82)

tutorial.en:
# Roll Counterclockwise

The camera only rolls counterclockwise without any other camera movement. A **roll** rotates the camera around its optical axis, tilting the horizon line so the right side rises and the left side dips.

Like clockwise roll, this movement conveys **disorientation or dreamlike instability**. Counterclockwise roll is sometimes chosen for its subtly different visual rhythm, or to match the direction of an on-screen rotation (a falling character, a spinning object).

- Related: [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:83)
tutorial.zh:
# 逆时针翻滚

相机仅绕光轴逆时针旋转，没有其他运动。画面右侧上升、左侧下降。

传达**迷失方向感或梦幻般的不稳定感**。

- 相关: [顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:14) | [荷兰角](taxonomy:82)

tutorial.en:
# Has Roll

The camera rolls (rotates around the optical axis) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_rotation classifiers) to identify any roll component.

- Related: [Has Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:305) | [Has Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:15)
tutorial.zh:
# 含翻滚

相机绕光轴旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。使用**存在性检测**识别任何翻滚分量。

- 相关: [含顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:305) | [含逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:15)

tutorial.en:
# Has Roll Clockwise

The camera rolls clockwise, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any clockwise rotation around the optical axis**.

- Related: [Has Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:15) | [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14)
tutorial.zh:
# 含顺时针翻滚

相机顺时针绕光轴旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:15) | [顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:14)

tutorial.en:
# Has Counterclockwise Roll Movement

The camera rolls counterclockwise at some point during the shot, potentially combined with other movements. This label detects **any counterclockwise roll component** in the camera's motion.

- Related: [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16) | [Has Roll Movement](taxonomy:13)
tutorial.zh:
# 含逆时针翻滚

相机逆时针绕光轴旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含顺时针翻滚](taxonomy:305) | [逆时针翻滚](taxonomy:16)

tutorial.en:
# Pan

The camera pans (rotates horizontally) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **pan** pivots the camera left or right on a fixed axis without physically displacing the camera body.

Panning is one of the most fundamental and frequently used camera movements in filmmaking, used to **survey a scene, follow lateral action, connect two subjects, or reveal off-screen space**. It ranges from slow, contemplative sweeps across a landscape to rapid whip-pans that serve as energetic transitions.

The term "pan" derives from "panorama," reflecting the movement's original purpose of capturing wide scenic views.

- Related: [Pan Left](taxonomy:8) | [Pan Right](taxonomy:10) | [Truck](taxonomy:5)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇镜

相机进行水平旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。**摇镜**在固定轴上左右转动，相机本身不位移。

摇镜是最基础的运镜手法之一，用于**扫视场景、跟随横向动作、连接两个主体或揭示画面外的空间**。甩镜（Whip Pan）——极快速的摇镜导致画面模糊——是常见的风格化转场手段。

- 相关: [左摇镜](taxonomy:8) | [右摇镜](taxonomy:10) | [横移](taxonomy:5)

tutorial.en:
# Pan Left

The camera only pans leftward without any other camera movement. A **pan** is a horizontal rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, sweeping the frame from right to left. Unlike a [Truck Left](taxonomy:6), the camera body stays in place and simply pivots.

Filmmakers use pan left to **follow a subject moving screen-left, reveal new information beside the current frame, or shift the audience's attention** from one part of a scene to another. A slow pan left can build anticipation, while a fast whip-pan creates an energetic transition.

The pan is one of the oldest deliberate camera movements, dating to the earliest days of cinema when operators hand-cranked cameras on tripod heads. Today it remains a fundamental building block of visual storytelling.

- Related: [Pan Right](taxonomy:10) | [Truck Left](taxonomy:6)
tutorial.zh:
# 左摇镜

相机仅向左进行水平旋转，没有其他运动。画面从右向左扫过。与[横移左](taxonomy:6)不同，相机本身不移动。

用于**跟随向左移动的主体、揭示画面旁边的新信息或转移观众注意力**。

- 相关: [右摇镜](taxonomy:10) | [横移左](taxonomy:6)

tutorial.en:
# Pan Right

The camera only pans rightward without any other camera movement. A **pan** is a horizontal rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, sweeping the frame from left to right. Unlike a [Truck Right](taxonomy:12), the camera body stays in place and simply pivots.

Filmmakers use pan right to **follow a subject moving screen-right, survey a landscape, or guide the viewer's eye** toward a new point of interest. In Western cultures, where reading flows left-to-right, a rightward pan can feel natural and progressive.

- Related: [Pan Left](taxonomy:8) | [Truck Right](taxonomy:12)
tutorial.zh:
# 右摇镜

相机仅向右进行水平旋转，没有其他运动。画面从左向右扫过。与[横移右](taxonomy:12)不同，相机本身不移动。

用于**跟随向右移动的主体或将视线引导向新的关注点**。

- 相关: [左摇镜](taxonomy:8) | [横移右](taxonomy:12)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pan

The camera pans (rotates horizontally) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_rotation classifiers) to identify any pan component in the camera's motion, whether the pan is the sole movement or part of a complex compound motion.

Unlike the [Pan](taxonomy:7) label in Camera Movement (which uses exclusion-based Only classifiers), this label directly tests for the presence of horizontal rotation using dedicated has-detection classifiers.

- Related: [Has Pan Left](taxonomy:301) | [Has Pan Right](taxonomy:9)
tutorial.zh:
# 含摇镜

相机进行水平旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。使用**存在性检测**识别任何摇镜分量。

与[摇镜](taxonomy:7)标签（使用排他性分类器）不同，此标签直接检测水平旋转的存在，无论是否为唯一运动。

- 相关: [含左摇镜](taxonomy:301) | [含右摇镜](taxonomy:9)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pan Left

The camera pans to the left, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any leftward horizontal rotation** regardless of whether it occurs in isolation or as part of a compound movement.

- Related: [Has Pan Right](taxonomy:9) | [Pan Left](taxonomy:8)
tutorial.zh:
# 含左摇镜

相机向左进行水平旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。检测**任何向左的水平旋转分量**。

- 相关: [含右摇镜](taxonomy:9) | [左摇镜](taxonomy:8)

tutorial.en:
# Has Pan Right Movement

The camera pans to the right at some point during the shot, potentially combined with other movements. This label detects **any rightward pan component** in the camera's motion.

- Related: [Pan Right](taxonomy:10) | [Has Pan Movement](taxonomy:7)
tutorial.zh:
# 含右摇镜

相机向右进行水平旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。检测**任何向右的水平旋转分量**。

- 相关: [含左摇镜](taxonomy:301) | [右摇镜](taxonomy:10)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt

The camera tilts (rotates vertically) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **tilt** angles the camera up or down on a fixed axis without physically raising or lowering the camera body.

Tilting is used to **reveal vertical space, follow rising or falling action, survey tall structures, or shift between a character's face and hands**. It is the vertical counterpart of the pan and equally fundamental to camera grammar.

- Related: [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Pedestal](taxonomy:36)
tutorial.zh:
# 俯仰

相机进行垂直旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。**俯仰**在固定轴上向上或向下改变角度，相机本身不升降。

用于**展示垂直空间、跟随上升或下落的动作、扫视高大建筑**。它是摇镜的垂直对应。

- 相关: [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [下俯](taxonomy:18) | [升降](taxonomy:36)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt Up

The camera only tilts upward without any other camera movement. A **tilt** is a vertical rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, angling the lens upward while the camera body remains stationary. Unlike a [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) or [Crane Up](taxonomy:4), the camera does not physically rise.

Filmmakers tilt up to **reveal height, convey power or grandeur, or follow a subject rising**. A classic use is the slow tilt up a skyscraper facade to emphasize scale. In character work, tilting up from feet to face can build mystery or introduce a figure with dramatic weight.

Alfred Hitchcock and Orson Welles frequently used exaggerated tilt angles to create psychological tension, pairing tilt with low-angle framing.

- Related: [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Crane Up](taxonomy:4)
tutorial.zh:
# 上仰

相机仅向上进行垂直旋转，没有其他运动。与[升](taxonomy:38)或[垂直弧形升](taxonomy:4)不同，相机不进行物理位移。

用于**展示高度、传达力量感或宏伟感，或跟随上升的主体**。

- 相关: [下俯](taxonomy:18) | [升](taxonomy:38) | [垂直弧形升](taxonomy:4)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt Down

The camera only tilts downward without any other camera movement. A **tilt** is a vertical rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, angling the lens downward while the camera body remains stationary. Unlike a [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) or [Crane Down](taxonomy:3), the camera does not physically descend.

Filmmakers tilt down to **reveal what lies below the current frame, show a character's point of view looking downward, or create a sense of vulnerability**. A slow tilt down from sky to ground can establish setting, while a sudden tilt down can direct attention to a critical detail on the floor or table.

- Related: [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
# 下俯

相机仅向下进行垂直旋转，没有其他运动。与[降](taxonomy:32)或[垂直弧形降](taxonomy:3)不同，相机不进行物理位移。

用于**揭示画面下方的内容、展示角色向下看的视角或营造脆弱感**。

- 相关: [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [降](taxonomy:32) | [垂直弧形降](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Has Tilt

The camera tilts (rotates vertically) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_rotation classifiers) to identify any tilt component in the camera's motion.

- Related: [Has Tilt Up](taxonomy:303) | [Has Tilt Down](taxonomy:17)
tutorial.zh:
# 含俯仰

相机进行垂直旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。使用**存在性检测**识别任何俯仰分量。

- 相关: [含上仰](taxonomy:303) | [含下俯](taxonomy:17)

tutorial.en:
# Has Tilt Up

The camera tilts upward, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any upward vertical rotation** regardless of whether other movements are present.

- Related: [Has Tilt Down](taxonomy:17) | [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20)
tutorial.zh:
# 含上仰

相机向上进行垂直旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含下俯](taxonomy:17) | [上仰](taxonomy:20)

tutorial.en:
# Has Tilt Down Movement

The camera tilts downward at some point during the shot, potentially combined with other movements. This label detects **any downward tilt component** in the camera's motion.

- Related: [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Has Tilt Movement](taxonomy:19)
tutorial.zh:
# 含下俯

相机向下进行垂直旋转，可能同时伴随其他运动。

- 相关: [含上仰](taxonomy:303) | [下俯](taxonomy:18)

tutorial.en:
# Zoom

The camera zooms (changes focal length) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **zoom** magnifies or widens the view without physically moving the camera, changing the field of view while keeping the camera's position fixed.

Zooms alter framing without introducing parallax, giving them a distinctive "flat" quality compared to dolly movements. They are used to **draw attention to a detail, create dramatic emphasis, or smoothly reframe within a continuous shot**.

- Related: [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly](taxonomy:33)
tutorial.zh:
# 变焦

相机进行变焦（改变焦距），可能同时伴随其他运动。**变焦**通过改变焦距放大或缩小视野，相机本身不动。

变焦不引入视差，呈现与推拉截然不同的「平面」质感。

- 相关: [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [推拉](taxonomy:33)

tutorial.en:
# Zoom In

The camera only zooms in with no other movement. A **zoom** changes the lens focal length, magnifying the center of the frame without physically moving the camera. The result narrows the field of view and brings distant subjects closer.

Unlike a [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35), a zoom does not change the camera's physical position, so the perspective relationship between foreground and background objects stays the same. This gives zooms a distinctive "flat" feel compared to the parallax shift of a dolly.

Zooms became ubiquitous in the 1960s and 1970s with directors like Robert Altman and Sergio Leone, who used long, creeping zooms to isolate characters or objects. Stanley Kubrick's slow zoom in [*Barry Lyndon* (1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Lyndon) and the snap-zoom in [*The Shining* (1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film)) are celebrated examples.

- Related: [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25)
tutorial.zh:
# 变焦推进

相机仅进行变焦推入，没有其他运动。通过改变焦距放大画面中心，视野收窄。

与[推](taxonomy:35)不同，变焦不改变物理位置，不引入视差。变焦在1960至1970年代广泛流行。

- 相关: [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [推](taxonomy:35) | [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)

tutorial.en:
# Zoom Out

The camera only zooms out with no other movement. A **zoom out** widens the lens focal length, expanding the field of view and making the subject appear to recede into a broader context.

Filmmakers use zoom outs to **reveal surroundings, create a sense of isolation, or transition from an intimate detail to a wider establishing view**. A slow zoom out from a character's face can suggest emotional distance or loneliness, while a rapid zoom out can deliver a comedic or shocking reveal of unexpected scale.

- Related: [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 变焦拉远

相机仅进行变焦拉出，没有其他运动。扩大焦距，拓展视野。

用于**揭示周围环境、营造孤立感或从细节过渡到全景**。

- 相关: [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [拉](taxonomy:29) | [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Has Zoom

The camera zooms (changes focal length) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This label uses **presence-based detection** (has_intrinsic_change classifiers) to identify any zoom component.

- Related: [Has Zoom In](taxonomy:307) | [Has Zoom Out](taxonomy:23)

tutorial.en:

The camera zooms in (narrows focal length), potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. This detects **any zoom-in component** regardless of whether other movements are present.

- Related: [Has Zoom Out](taxonomy:23) | [Zoom In](taxonomy:22)
