tutorial.en:
# Dolly Zoom

The camera performs a dolly zoom effect (combining physical dolly movement with simultaneous opposing zoom) in any direction. The **dolly zoom** (also called the **Vertigo effect**) produces a distinctive warping of background perspective while keeping the subject roughly the same size in frame.

First popularized by Alfred Hitchcock in [*Vertigo* (1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film)), the technique conveys **psychological realization, shock, or disorientation**. It has since appeared in iconic scenes in [*Jaws* (1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(film)) and [*The Lord of the Rings* (2001)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series)).

- Related: [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25) | [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 滑动变焦

相机同时进行物理推拉和反向变焦。**滑动变焦**（又称眩晕效果）在保持主体大小不变的同时，使背景透视发生剧烈扭曲。

由希区柯克在[《迷魂记》(1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film))中首次推广，传达**心理觉醒、震惊或迷失方向感**。

- 相关: [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25) | [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Zoom In

The **dolly zoom in** (also called the **Vertigo effect**) combines a forward dolly movement with a simultaneous zoom out. The background appears to stretch away from the subject, producing a strong sense of **spatial unease**. A common variant keeps the subject roughly the same size in frame while the background warps dramatically around them.

Filmmakers use this technique to convey **psychological realization, shock, or disorientation**  making it a go-to tool for moments of sudden emotional shift. First popularized by Alfred Hitchcock in [*Vertigo* (1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film)), the effect has since appeared in iconic scenes in [*Jaws* (1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(film)) and [*The Lord of the Rings* (2001)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series)).

- Related technique: [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 滑动变焦推进

向前推轨同时变焦拉远。背景看似从主体身后急剧拉伸，产生强烈的**空间不安感**。

希区柯克[《迷魂记》(1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film))和斯皮尔伯格[《大白鲨》(1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(film))中均有经典运用。

- 相关: [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Zoom Out

The camera performs a dolly zoom effect with backward movement and zoom-in. This is the **reverse Vertigo effect**: the camera pulls backward while simultaneously zooming in, keeping the subject roughly the same size but causing the **background to appear to compress and close in** behind them.

Where the [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25) stretches the background away to convey shock or realization, the dolly zoom out pushes the background forward, creating a sense of **claustrophobia, entrapment, or mounting pressure**. The technique can make a space feel like it is shrinking around the subject.

Though less commonly used than its forward counterpart, the reverse dolly zoom appears in films like [*Goodfellas* (1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas), where Martin Scorsese used it in the famous diner scene to suggest paranoia closing in.

- Related: [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25)
tutorial.zh:
# 滑动变焦拉出

向后推轨同时变焦推入。背景看似被压缩并向主体逼近，营造**幽闭感和压迫感**。

斯科塞斯在[《好家伙》(1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas)的餐厅场景中以此暗示偏执感的逼近。

- 相关: [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)

tutorial.en:
# Arc

The camera arcs (orbits) around the subject in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. An **arc shot** moves the camera along a curved path around a subject while keeping the subject in frame.

Filmmakers use arc shots to **add visual dynamism, reveal multiple sides of a subject, convey psychological tension, or emphasize a pivotal moment in dialogue**. Famous arc shots include the circling camera in [*Goodfellas*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas) and the bullet-time orbit in [*The Matrix* (1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix).

- Related: [Arc Clockwise](taxonomy:1) | [Arc Counterclockwise](taxonomy:2)
tutorial.zh:
# 水平弧形镜

相机沿水平弧形路径绕主体运动，可能同时伴随其他运动。

水平弧形镜用于**增加视觉动感、展示主体多个侧面、传达心理张力**。[《黑客帝国》(1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix)的子弹时间是最经典的水平弧形镜。

- 相关: [顺时针水平弧形镜](taxonomy:1) | [逆时针水平弧形镜](taxonomy:2)

tutorial.en:
# Arc Clockwise

The camera arcs clockwise around the subject. An **arc shot** (or **orbit shot**) moves the camera along a curved path around a subject while keeping the subject in frame. The camera appears to move toward the left side of the frame, while from a top-down perspective, it follows a clockwise arc. 

Filmmakers use arc shots to **add visual dynamism, reveal multiple sides of a subject, convey psychological tension, or emphasize a pivotal moment in dialogue**. A slow arc can create intimacy and dimensionality, while a fast orbit can heighten drama or disorientation. The arc also reveals depth in a scene by continuously changing the parallax relationship between subject and background.

Famous arc shots include the circling camera in the restaurant scene of [*Goodfellas*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas), and the iconic 360-degree orbit in [*The Matrix* (1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix) (achieved with the bullet-time rig).

- Related: [Arc Counterclockwise](taxonomy:2)
tutorial.zh:
# 顺时针水平弧形镜

相机顺时针绕主体做水平弧形运动（相机看起来是朝画面左边移动，从上方看相机顺时针移动）。

用于**增加视觉动感、展示主体多个侧面或强调对话中的关键时刻**。

- 相关: [逆时针水平弧形镜](taxonomy:2)

tutorial.en:
# Arc Counterclockwise

The camera arcs counterclockwise around the subject. An **arc shot** moves the camera along a curved path around a subject. The camera appears to move toward the right side of the frame, while from a top-down perspective, it follows a counterclockwise arc.

Arc direction is typically chosen to match blocking, reveal key background elements at the right moment, or complement the emotional arc of the scene. Counterclockwise arcs can feel subtly different in rhythm from clockwise ones, and directors often choose direction based on which side of the subject they want to reveal first.

- Related: [Arc Clockwise](taxonomy:1)
tutorial.zh:
# 逆时针水平弧形镜

相机逆时针绕主体做水平弧形运动（相机看起来是朝画面右边移动，从上方看相机逆时针移动）。

弧形方向通常根据场面调度选择，以配合情感弧线或揭示背景元素。

- 相关: [顺时针水平弧形镜](taxonomy:1)

# Crane

The camera cranes (moves along a curved vertical arc) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **crane shot** uses a jib or crane arm to move the camera along an arcing vertical path, simultaneously changing height and viewing angle.

Crane shots are used for **sweeping reveals, establishing geography, and creating a sense of transcendence or descent**. They date to the 1930s and became iconic through films like [*Gone with the Wind* (1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film)).

- Related: [Crane Up](taxonomy:4) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
# 垂直弧形镜

相机沿垂直弧形路径运动（摇臂），可能同时伴随其他运动。

垂直弧形镜用于**全景展示、建立地理环境和营造超越或下沉感**。

- 相关: [垂直弧形升镜](taxonomy:4) | [垂直弧形降镜](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Crane Up

The camera cranes upward in an arc relative to its own frame. A **crane up** moves the camera along a curved vertical path, typically pivoting on a jib or crane arm. Unlike a straight [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38), the crane produces an arcing trajectory where the camera simultaneously rises and changes its viewing angle.

Filmmakers use crane up shots for **sweeping reveals, establishing geography from above, and creating a sense of liberation or transcendence**. A crane up at the end of a scene often conveys release, escape, or an emotional widening of perspective.

Crane shots date to the 1930s with early mechanical jibs, but became iconic through films like [*Gone with the Wind* (1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film)), which featured a legendary crane-up over wounded soldiers in Atlanta. Modern telescoping cranes and drone rigs can achieve even more dramatic vertical arcs.

- Related: [Crane Down](taxonomy:3) | [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38)
tutorial.zh:
# 垂直弧形升镜

相机沿垂直弧形路径向上升起，同时改变视角。与直线[升镜](taxonomy:38)不同，垂直弧形升镜遵循弧形轨迹。

用于**全景揭示、从高处建立地理环境或营造解放和超越感**。

- 相关: [垂直弧形降镜](taxonomy:3) | [升镜](taxonomy:38)

tutorial.en:
# Crane Down

The camera cranes downward in an arc relative to its own frame. A **crane down** follows a curved descending path, simultaneously lowering the camera and adjusting its angle. Unlike a straight [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32), the arcing motion adds a sweeping quality.

Filmmakers use crane down to **descend into a scene, move from an establishing overview to an intimate ground-level perspective, or create a feeling of descending weight or gravity**. Opening a scene with a crane down from above can elegantly transition from context to character.

- Related: [Crane Up](taxonomy:4) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32)
tutorial.zh:
# 垂直弧形降镜

相机沿垂直弧形路径向下降落，同时改变视角。与直线[降镜](taxonomy:32)不同，垂直弧形降镜遵循弧形轨迹。

用于**进入场景、从全景概览过渡到地面视角或营造重力下沉感**。

- 相关: [垂直弧形升镜](taxonomy:4) | [降镜](taxonomy:32)

tutorial.en:

tutorial.en:
# Tracking Shot

The camera tracks the subject as they move. A **tracking shot** follows a moving subject through space, keeping them in frame as they walk, run, drive, or otherwise travel. The camera may translate, pan, tilt, or combine movements to maintain the subject's position in the composition.

Tracking shots are among the most versatile tools in filmmaking, used to **build intimacy with a character, sustain tension across a continuous take, or immerse the audience in the subject's journey**. The technique can feel invisible when executed smoothly, or deliberately conspicuous as a bravura long take.

One of the most celebrated tracking shots in cinema history is the Copacabana scene in [*Goodfellas* (1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas), where the camera follows Henry and Karen through a restaurant's back entrance in a single unbroken shot. Orson Welles' opening crane-track in [*Touch of Evil* (1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_of_Evil) set the standard for virtuoso tracking.

- Related: [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44) | [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50) | [Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:47)
tutorial.zh:
# 跟踪镜头

相机跟随移动的主体，使其始终保持在画面中。相机可能通过平移、摇镜、俯仰或组合运动来维持主体在构图中的位置。

跟踪镜头用于**与角色建立亲密感、维持连续长镜头中的张力或让观众沉浸在主体的旅程中**。[《好家伙》(1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas)中穿越餐厅后门的一镜到底是影史上最经典的跟踪镜头之一。

- 相关: [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44) | [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Lead Tracking Shot

A lead tracking shot where the camera moves ahead of the subject, traveling in the same direction as they approach the camera. The camera faces the subject and retreats before them, keeping the subject's face (or front) visible.

Lead tracking is essential for **dialogue scenes in motion, character introductions, and moments where the audience needs to read the subject's expression**. By showing the subject head-on while they advance, the shot creates a sense of direct engagement between character and viewer. It can also build anticipation: the viewer sees where the character is headed only when the camera finally reveals the background.

The technique is common in Steadicam work, where the operator walks backward ahead of the actor.

- Related: [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50) | [Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:47)
tutorial.zh:
# 前引跟踪

相机在主体前方移动，面向主体后退拍摄，保持主体正面可见。

对于**运动中的对话场景和角色介绍**至关重要——通过正面展示角色面貌建立直接的互动感。

- 相关: [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Follow Tracking Shot

A follow tracking shot where the camera moves behind the subject, traveling in the same direction as they move away from the camera. The camera sees the subject's back and follows them into the scene.

Follow shots create a feeling of **accompanying the character on their journey**. The viewer shares the character's forward momentum and discovers the environment at the same pace. This perspective is widely used in action sequences, walk-and-talk scenes, and horror films where the unseen threat is implied by the camera's position behind the character.

The Dardenne brothers are known for extended follow shots that stay glued to a character's back, creating visceral intimacy.

- Related: [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44) | [Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:47)
tutorial.zh:
# 后随跟踪

相机在主体后方移动，拍摄主体的背影并跟随其进入场景。

营造**陪伴角色旅程**的感觉。常用于动作场景和恐怖片——相机位于角色身后暗示着看不见的威胁。

- 相关: [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Side Tracking Shot

A side tracking shot with the camera moving from the side to follow the moving subject. The camera travels parallel to the subject's path of motion, keeping them in profile.

Side tracking is a staple of **dialogue walks, running sequences, and any scene requiring sustained lateral movement**. The profile view lets the audience observe both the subject and the environment passing behind them. It often conveys a sense of progression or journey.

Classic side tracking shots run along dolly rails laid parallel to a street or corridor. Modern gimbals and vehicle rigs allow longer and more dynamic lateral tracks.

- Related: [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44) | [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50)
tutorial.zh:
# 侧面跟踪

相机从侧面与主体平行移动，保持侧面视角。

**对话行走、奔跑场景和需要持续横向运动**的标准手法。侧面视角让观众能同时观察主体和经过的环境。

- 相关: [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44) | [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50)

tutorial.en: A side tracking shot where the camera moves left to follow the subject.
tutorial.zh:
# 侧面跟踪（向左）

相机向左移动以侧面跟随主体。

- 相关: [侧面跟踪（向右）](taxonomy:49) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en: A side tracking shot where the camera moves right to follow the subject.
tutorial.zh:
# 侧面跟踪（向右）

相机向右移动以侧面跟随主体。

- 相关: [侧面跟踪（向左）](taxonomy:48) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Front-Side Tracking Shot

A front-side tracking shot where the camera leads the moving subject from a front-side angle. The camera is positioned ahead and to one side of the subject, showing a three-quarter front view as they move forward.

This angle provides a **compromise between the intimacy of a lead shot and the spatial context of a side shot**. The subject's face is partially visible, and the viewer can see both where the subject is heading and how the environment unfolds beside them. It is common in action films and documentary-style shooting.

- Related: [Rear-Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:46) | [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44)
tutorial.zh:
# 前侧跟踪

相机从前侧角度引领移动的主体，展示四分之三正面视角。

提供**前引镜头的亲密感与侧面镜头的空间感之间的折中**。

- 相关: [后侧跟踪](taxonomy:46) | [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44)

tutorial.en:
# Rear-Side Tracking Shot

A rear-side tracking shot where the camera follows the moving subject at a rear-side angle. The camera is positioned behind and to one side of the subject, showing a three-quarter rear view.

This angle offers a **sense of shadowing the character** while still revealing some environment ahead. It is frequently used in **pursuit sequences and stealth scenarios**, where the camera's oblique rear position mimics the feeling of someone trailing the subject.

- Related: [Front-Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:43) | [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50)
tutorial.zh:
# 后侧跟踪

相机从后侧角度跟随移动的主体，展示四分之三背面视角。

营造**尾随角色**的感觉。常用于追逐和潜行场景。

- 相关: [前侧跟踪](taxonomy:43) | [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50)

tutorial.en:
# Aerial Tracking Shot

An aerial tracking shot where the camera follows the moving subject from an aerial view. The camera is positioned high above, typically from a drone or helicopter, and moves to keep the subject in frame as they traverse the landscape below.

Aerial tracking shots provide a **god's-eye perspective on movement through space**, revealing geography, terrain, and the subject's relationship to their surroundings in ways ground-level shots cannot. They are commonly used in chase sequences, travel montages, and establishing shots of characters moving through expansive environments.

Once requiring expensive helicopter rigs, aerial tracking has become far more accessible with consumer and cinema drones since the 2010s.

- Related: [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52) | [Drone POV](taxonomy:165)
tutorial.zh:
# 航拍跟踪

相机从高空俯瞰并跟随移动的主体，通常由无人机或直升机承载。

提供**上帝视角的运动透视**，揭示地形和主体与环境的关系。常用于追逐场景和旅途段落。

- 相关: [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52) | [航拍视角](taxonomy:165)

tutorial.en:
# Arc Tracking Shot

An arc tracking shot where the camera follows the moving subject while arcing around them. The camera simultaneously tracks the subject's movement and orbits around them, combining lateral travel with a curved path.

This creates a **highly dynamic, three-dimensional feel** that reveals both the subject and their environment from shifting angles. Arc tracking shots are used for **dramatic confrontations, dance sequences, and action set-pieces** where the filmmaker wants to maintain continuous visual engagement while showing multiple facets of the scene.

- Related: [Arc Clockwise](taxonomy:1) | [Arc Counterclockwise](taxonomy:2) | [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52)
tutorial.zh:
# 弧形跟踪

相机在跟随移动主体的同时绕其做弧形运动，将横向跟踪与弧形环绕结合。

制造**极具动感的三维效果**，从不断变化的角度展示主体和环境。

- 相关: [顺时针弧形](taxonomy:1) | [逆时针弧形](taxonomy:2) | [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52)

tutorial.en:
# Pan Tracking Shot

The camera pans to track the moving subjects. Rather than translating through space, the camera stays in one position and **rotates horizontally to follow the subject's movement** across the frame.

Pan tracking is the simplest form of subject-following and works well when the subject moves laterally past the camera at a moderate distance. It is commonly used in **sports coverage, surveillance-style sequences, and any scene where the camera cannot or should not physically move**. The technique keeps the subject framed without revealing depth or parallax.

- Related: [Tilt Tracking Shot](taxonomy:51) | [Pan Left](taxonomy:8) | [Pan Right](taxonomy:10)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇镜跟踪

相机保持固定位置，仅通过水平旋转跟随主体的横向运动。

最简单的跟随方式，适用于主体在中等距离处横向经过的场景。不产生视差。

- 相关: [俯仰跟踪](taxonomy:51) | [左摇镜](taxonomy:8) | [右摇镜](taxonomy:10)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt Tracking Shot

The camera tilts to track the moving subjects. The camera stays in one position and **rotates vertically to follow the subject** as they move up or down in the frame.

Tilt tracking is used when a subject ascends stairs, climbs a wall, jumps, or falls. It can also follow a subject rising from seated to standing. The technique is simpler than a crane or pedestal move but effective for **maintaining focus on vertical motion without requiring physical camera displacement**.

- Related: [Pan Tracking Shot](taxonomy:45) | [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18)
tutorial.zh:
# 俯仰跟踪

相机保持固定位置，仅通过垂直旋转跟随主体的上下运动。

用于主体上楼梯、攀爬、跳跃或坠落等场景。

- 相关: [摇镜跟踪](taxonomy:45) | [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [下俯](taxonomy:18)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Getting Larger

The subject appears larger during the tracking shot. As the camera tracks a subject, the subject's size in frame **increases over the duration of the shot**, indicating the camera is closing the distance or the subject is approaching.

This technique builds **intensity, intimacy, or confrontation**. A tracking shot where the subject steadily grows larger can create a sense of the audience being drawn into the subject's world, or of tension escalating as the camera pushes in during pursuit or approach.

- Related: [Subject Getting Smaller](taxonomy:54) | [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体趋近

跟踪镜头中主体在画面中逐渐变大，表明相机正在缩短距离。

增强**紧张感、亲密感或对抗感**。

- 相关: [主体趋远](taxonomy:54) | [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Getting Smaller

The subject appears smaller during the tracking shot. As the camera tracks a subject, the subject's size in frame **decreases over the duration**, indicating the camera is falling behind or the subject is moving away.

This creates a sense of **separation, loss, or helplessness**. A shrinking subject during a tracking shot can convey abandonment, a character's isolation, or the futility of pursuit.

- Related: [Subject Getting Larger](taxonomy:53) | [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体趋远

跟踪镜头中主体在画面中逐渐变小，表明相机正在落后或主体正在远离。

营造**分离感、失落感或无助感**。

- 相关: [主体趋近](taxonomy:53) | [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52)

tutorial.en:
# Smooth Motion

The video has exceptionally smooth and highly stable camera movement. **Smooth motion** is typically achieved with a Steadicam, gimbal, dolly track, or slider. The absence of vibration keeps the audience's attention on the subject and composition rather than the camera itself.

The Steadicam, invented by Garrett Brown in 1975, revolutionized cinema by enabling smooth, fluid movement through complex environments. Its debut in [*Rocky* (1976)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_(film)) and [*The Shining* (1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film)) demonstrated that a camera could glide through spaces with an almost ghostly precision.

- Related: [Shaky Motion](taxonomy:60) | [Completely Still](taxonomy:57)
tutorial.zh:
# 平稳运镜

相机运动极其平稳流畅，通常通过斯坦尼康、电子云台、推轨或滑轨实现。

斯坦尼康由加雷特·布朗于1975年发明，在[《洛奇》(1976)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_(film))和[《闪灵》(1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film))中的首次亮相展示了相机可以幽灵般地滑行穿越复杂环境。

- 相关: [明显抖动](taxonomy:60) | [完全静止](taxonomy:57)

tutorial.en:
# Shaky Motion

The video shows noticeable vibrations, shaking, or wobbling of the camera. **Shaky camera work** (or shaky-cam) can be intentional or incidental. When used deliberately, it conveys **raw immediacy, documentary realism, or a character's subjective agitation**.

The technique gained mainstream prominence through films like [*Saving Private Ryan* (1998)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving_Private_Ryan), where Janusz Kaminski's handheld cinematography placed viewers in the visceral chaos of combat. The found-footage genre ([*The Blair Witch Project*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blair_Witch_Project), [*Cloverfield*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloverfield)) relies on shaky motion as its core aesthetic.

- Related: [Smooth Motion](taxonomy:61) | [Handheld Shake](taxonomy:58)
tutorial.zh:
# 明显抖动

相机有明显的振动、抖动或晃动。可以是有意的也可以是偶然的。

当刻意使用时传达**原始的即时感、纪录片式的真实感或角色的主观焦躁**。[《拯救大兵瑞恩》(1998)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving_Private_Ryan)的诺曼底登陆场景是经典范例。

- 相关: [平稳运镜](taxonomy:61) | [手持微晃](taxonomy:58)

tutorial.en:
# Completely Still

The video shows a completely still camera with no motion or shaking. A **locked-off camera** is mounted on a tripod (or other rigid support) with no movement at all. This is the most neutral camera state, directing all attention to what happens within the frame.

Directors like Wes Anderson and Yasujiro Ozu are celebrated for their disciplined use of static frames. Anderson's symmetrical compositions and Ozu's low-angle tatami shots derive much of their visual power from the camera's absolute stillness, letting composition and blocking carry the storytelling.

- Related: [Handheld Shake](taxonomy:58) | [Smooth Motion](taxonomy:61)
tutorial.zh:
# 完全静止

相机完全静止，安装在三脚架或固定支架上，绝对不动。

将所有视觉注意力集中于**场景本身的内部运动**。韦斯·安德森和小津安二郎以对静态构图的严谨使用而闻名。

- 相关: [手持微晃](taxonomy:58) | [平稳运镜](taxonomy:61)

tutorial.en:
# Handheld Shake

The video has a mostly stationary camera with only minor vibrations or shaking. **Handheld shake** falls between a locked-off tripod shot and deliberate shaky-cam. The camera is largely still but exhibits the subtle, organic tremor of a human operator.

This look is common in **dialogue-driven dramas and documentaries**, where it adds a sense of presence and immediacy without the disorienting intensity of full shaky-cam. Many cinematographers intentionally shoot handheld even on static setups to inject a subtle sense of life into the frame.

- Related: [Completely Still](taxonomy:57) | [Shaky Motion](taxonomy:60)
tutorial.zh:
# 手持微晃

相机基本静止，仅有操作者手持产生的细微有机颤动。

介于锁定机位和刻意手持抖动之间。在**对话剧情片和纪录片**中常见，增添一丝人的临场感而不会引起视觉不适。

- 相关: [完全静止](taxonomy:57) | [明显抖动](taxonomy:60)

tutorial.en:
# Fast Moving Camera

The camera has noticeable motion at a fast speed. **Fast camera movement** creates energy, urgency, and kinetic excitement. It can convey a character's rush, the chaos of an action sequence, or the exhilaration of speed.

Directors like Michael Bay and the Russo Brothers use rapid camera movement as a signature style in action filmmaking. Fast pans (whip pans) are also used as **transitions** between scenes or time periods, snapping from one composition to the next.

- Related: [Slowly Moving Camera](taxonomy:59) | [Motion Blur](taxonomy:40)
tutorial.zh:
# 快速运镜

相机以快速速度进行明显运动。

制造**能量感、紧迫感和动态冲击力**。快速摇镜（甩镜）也常被用作场景之间的过渡手段。

- 相关: [慢速运镜](taxonomy:59) | [运动模糊](taxonomy:40)

tutorial.en:
# Slowly Moving Camera

The camera has noticeable motion at a slow speed. **Slow camera movement** builds atmosphere, draws attention to subtle details, and creates a contemplative or suspenseful mood. A creeping dolly or a glacial pan forces the audience to absorb the frame gradually.

Directors like Andrei Tarkovsky and Terrence Malick are known for extended slow camera movements that evoke meditative or dreamlike states. Stanley Kubrick's slow Steadicam tracking in [*The Shining* (1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film)) built unbearable tension through deliberate, unhurried forward motion.

- Related: [Fast Moving Camera](taxonomy:56) | [Smooth Motion](taxonomy:61)
tutorial.zh:
# 慢速运镜

相机以慢速进行明显运动。

营造**氛围、引导观众关注细微细节，创造沉思或悬疑的情绪**。库布里克在[《闪灵》(1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film))中的缓慢斯坦尼康跟踪是经典范例。

- 相关: [快速运镜](taxonomy:56) | [平稳运镜](taxonomy:61)

tutorial.en:
# Clearly Moving Camera

The video has noticeable camera motion beyond minor shake or wobble. This is a **broad motion detector** that identifies any video where the camera clearly moves, regardless of movement type or direction.

- Related: [Fast Moving Camera](taxonomy:56) | [Slowly Moving Camera](taxonomy:59)
tutorial.zh:
# 明显运镜

相机有超出轻微抖动的明显运动。

**广义运动检测**标签，识别任何相机明确运动的视频。

- 相关: [快速运镜](taxonomy:56) | [慢速运镜](taxonomy:59)

tutorial.en:
# Deep Focus

The camera uses a deep depth of field with distant details remaining sharp. **Everything in the frame from foreground to background is in sharp focus**, achieved through small apertures, wide-angle lenses, or strong lighting; however, in scenes with extensive depth, the foreground may appear slightly blurred.

Deep focus allows the audience to **scan the entire frame and choose where to look**, giving the filmmaker less control over attention but more compositional richness. Gregg Toland's cinematography for Orson Welles' [*Citizen Kane* (1941)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_Kane) pioneered deep focus as a narrative tool, staging significant action at multiple depth planes simultaneously.

- Related: [Shallow Focus](taxonomy:110) | [Ultra Shallow Focus](taxonomy:111)
tutorial.zh:
# 深焦

画面从前景到背景全部清晰合焦，通过小光圈、广角镜头或强照明实现。然而，在景深本身较大的场景中，前景可能会略显模糊。

深焦让观众可以**自由扫视整个画面**。威尔斯在[《公民凯恩》(1941)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_Kane)中开创了深焦作为叙事工具的先河。

- 相关: [浅焦](taxonomy:110) | [极浅焦](taxonomy:111)

tutorial.en:
# Shallow Focus

The camera uses shallow depth of field, with a limited but noticeable range of space in focus. The subject is sharp while foreground or background elements are **noticeably blurred**, guiding the viewer's eye to the plane of focus.

Shallow focus is one of cinema's primary tools for **directing attention, separating subjects from backgrounds, and creating aesthetic beauty**. It is achieved through wide apertures and longer focal lengths. The technique has become increasingly popular in digital filmmaking, where larger sensors enable shallower depth of field.

- Related: [Deep Focus](taxonomy:107) | [Ultra Shallow Focus](taxonomy:111) | [Rack Focus](taxonomy:109)
tutorial.zh:
# 浅焦

画面只有有限范围清晰合焦，主体清晰而前景或背景**明显虚化**。

电影中**引导注意力、分离主体与背景**的主要手段之一。

- 相关: [深焦](taxonomy:107) | [极浅焦](taxonomy:111) | [跟焦](taxonomy:109)

tutorial.en:
# Ultra Shallow Focus

The camera uses extremely shallow depth of field, with only a narrow plane in focus. The in-focus region is so thin that even **small movements can shift the subject out of sharpness**, and nearly everything except the precise focal point is blurred.

Ultra-shallow focus creates an **ethereal, dreamlike quality** and extreme subject isolation. It is a signature look in fashion photography, music videos, and art-house cinema. Achieving it requires fast lenses (f/1.2 or wider) or large-format sensors.

- Related: [Shallow Focus](taxonomy:110) | [Deep Focus](taxonomy:107) | [Bokeh](taxonomy:162)
tutorial.zh:
# 极浅焦

画面仅极窄平面合焦，合焦区域薄到**轻微移动即可使主体脱离清晰范围**。

制造**空灵、梦幻的画质**和极致的主体隔离。需要大光圈镜头或大画幅传感器。

- 相关: [浅焦](taxonomy:110) | [深焦](taxonomy:107)

tutorial.en:
# Rack Focus

The camera uses rack focus or pull focus to shift the focal plane. **Focus is deliberately pulled from one depth to another** during the shot, redirecting the viewer's attention between subjects or between foreground and background.

Rack focus is a powerful storytelling tool that **creates visual transitions without cutting, shifts audience attention between story elements, and can reveal narrative connections** between objects at different depths. A classic use is racking from a character in the foreground to someone approaching in the background.

The technique requires precise focus pulling, traditionally done by a dedicated focus puller (1st Assistant Camera) on the camera crew.

- Related: [Shallow Focus](taxonomy:110) | [Focus Change](taxonomy:93) | [Focus Tracking](taxonomy:108)
tutorial.zh:
# 跟焦

焦点在拍摄过程中**从一个深度平面移动到另一个**，引导观众注意力。

强大的叙事工具——**不间断地在不同故事元素之间转移注意力**。由专职跟焦员操作。

- 相关: [浅焦](taxonomy:110) | [焦点变化](taxonomy:93) | [焦点追踪](taxonomy:108)

tutorial.en:
# Foreground

The camera remains focused on the foreground using a shallow depth of field. The sharpest region of the image is the **plane closest to the camera**, with background elements blurred.

Foreground focus directs attention to **objects, hands, textures, or details closest to the lens** while abstracting the world behind them. It creates intimacy with nearby elements and can generate compositional depth through the contrast between sharp foreground and soft background.

- Related: [Middle Ground](taxonomy:106) | [Background](taxonomy:104)
tutorial.zh:
# 前景合焦

相机始终使用浅景深对焦于前景平面，背景虚化。

将注意力引向**距镜头最近的物体、手部或纹理**。

- 相关: [中景合焦](taxonomy:106) | [背景合焦](taxonomy:104)

tutorial.en:
# Middle Ground

The camera remains focused on the middle ground, keeping the foreground and background blurred. The sharpest region sits at an **intermediate distance from the camera**, with both nearer and farther planes out of focus.

Middle-ground focus is the most common focal plane in narrative filmmaking, as it typically corresponds to where subjects are positioned. It creates a natural **layered depth effect** with soft foreground and background framing the sharp subject.

- Related: [Foreground](taxonomy:105) | [Background](taxonomy:104)
tutorial.zh:
# 中景合焦

相机始终对焦于中景区域，前景和背景均虚化。

叙事电影中**最常见的焦平面选择**——通常对应主体所在的位置。

- 相关: [前景合焦](taxonomy:105) | [背景合焦](taxonomy:104)

tutorial.en:
# Background

The camera remains focused on the background using a shallow depth of field. The sharpest region is the **plane farthest from the camera**, with foreground elements blurred.

Background focus is less common than foreground or middle-ground focus and is used for **specific narrative purposes**: revealing an approaching figure, emphasizing a distant landscape detail, or creating a sense of the foreground subject being out of touch with the world behind them.

- Related: [Foreground](taxonomy:105) | [Middle Ground](taxonomy:106)
tutorial.zh:
# 背景合焦

相机始终使用浅景深对焦于背景平面，前景虚化。

用于**揭示远处正在接近的人物或强调背景中的关键细节**。

- 相关: [前景合焦](taxonomy:105) | [中景合焦](taxonomy:106)

tutorial.en:
# Focus Change

The focal plane shifts noticeably between foreground, middle ground, or background regions. The **depth of the sharpest region moves** during the shot, redirecting where the viewer's eye naturally rests.

Focus changes are a fundamental tool for **guided storytelling within a continuous shot**, allowing filmmakers to shift attention without cutting. The technique ranges from subtle pull-focus adjustments to dramatic rack-focus transitions.

- Related: [Focus Change (Far →Near)](taxonomy:94) | [Focus Change (Near →Far)](taxonomy:96) | [Rack Focus](taxonomy:109)
tutorial.zh:
# 焦点变化

焦平面在前景、中景或背景之间明显移动。

**在连续镜头中进行引导式叙事**的基本工具。

- 相关: [焦点由远及近](taxonomy:94) | [焦点由近及远](taxonomy:96) | [跟焦](taxonomy:109)

tutorial.en:
# Focus Change (Far →Near)

The focal plane shifts from distant to close, moving between foreground, middle ground, or background. Focus **pulls from the background toward the camera**, bringing closer elements into sharpness.

This transition typically **shifts attention from context to detail**, from a background scene to a foreground subject, or reveals a closer element that was previously blurred and unnoticed.

- Related: [Focus Change (Near →Far)](taxonomy:96) | [Focus Change](taxonomy:93)
tutorial.zh:
# 焦点由远及近

焦平面从远处向近处移动，使更靠近的元素逐渐变得清晰。

通常**将注意力从背景转移到前景主体**。

- 相关: [焦点由近及远](taxonomy:96) | [焦点变化](taxonomy:93)

tutorial.en:
# Focus Change (Near →Far)

The focal plane shifts from close to distant, moving between foreground, middle ground, or background. Focus **pushes from the foreground toward the background**, bringing distant elements into sharpness.

This transition typically **opens up the scene from an intimate detail to a wider context**, or redirects attention from a foreground subject to something important happening in the background.

- Related: [Focus Change (Far →Near)](taxonomy:94) | [Focus Change](taxonomy:93)
tutorial.zh:
# 焦点由近及远

焦平面从近处向远处移动，使更远的元素逐渐变得清晰。

通常**从亲密细节展开至更广阔的背景**。

- 相关: [焦点由远及近](taxonomy:94) | [焦点变化](taxonomy:93)

tutorial.en:
# In Focus →Out of Focus

The camera starts in sharp focus and then shifts out of focus. The image **progressively loses sharpness**, transitioning from a clear view to a blurred one.

This technique is commonly used as a **visual fade or transition effect**, signaling the end of a scene, a character losing consciousness, or a shift into memory or dream. It creates a gentle visual dissolution.

- Related: [Out of Focus →In Focus](taxonomy:97)
tutorial.zh:
# 由实到虚

画面从清晰合焦逐渐变为整体失焦。

常用作**视觉淡出或转场效果**——暗示场景结束、角色失去意识或进入记忆。

- 相关: [由虚到实](taxonomy:97)

tutorial.en:
# Out of Focus →In Focus

The camera starts out of focus and then becomes in focus. The image **progressively sharpens**, transitioning from blur to clarity.

This technique is used as a **visual wake-up or arrival effect**, opening a scene with disorientation before resolving into clarity. It can simulate a character waking up, gaining awareness, or the audience being drawn into a new moment.

- Related: [In Focus →Out of Focus](taxonomy:95)
tutorial.zh:
# 由虚到实

画面从整体失焦逐渐变为清晰合焦。

用作**视觉苏醒或进入效果**——以模糊开场，结束为清晰画面。

- 相关: [由实到虚](taxonomy:95)

tutorial.en:
# Focus Tracking

The camera uses focus tracking to keep a subject in focus in the video. The focal plane **continuously adjusts to maintain sharpness on a moving subject**, compensating for changes in the subject's distance from the camera.

Focus tracking is essential for any shot where a subject moves toward or away from the camera with shallow depth of field. It requires skilled manual focus pulling or modern autofocus systems. Without it, a moving subject would drift in and out of sharpness, which is generally undesirable unless used for artistic effect.

- Related: [Rack Focus](taxonomy:109) | [Shallow Focus](taxonomy:110)
tutorial.zh:
# 焦点追踪

焦平面持续调整以保持移动主体的清晰合焦。

在浅景深下拍摄移动主体时**不可或缺**。需要熟练的手动跟焦操作或现代自动对焦系统。

- 相关: [跟焦](taxonomy:109) | [浅焦](taxonomy:110)

# Time-Lapse

A time-lapse video played forward at greatly accelerated speed (more than 3x real-time), showing time passing rapidly over a long period. Events that unfold over **minutes, hours, or days are compressed** into seconds.

Time-lapse reveals **patterns invisible to normal perception**: clouds racing across the sky, flowers blooming, cities pulsing between day and night, construction projects rising. The technique transforms temporal scale, making slow processes dramatic and visible.

Ron Fricke's [*Baraka* (1992)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baraka_(film)) and [*Samsara* (2011)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsara_(2011_film)) are landmark time-lapse films.

- Related: [Fast-Motion](taxonomy:225) | [Regular Speed](taxonomy:227)
tutorial.zh:
# 延时摄影

以大幅加速（超过3倍实时速度）播放，展示长时间段内时间的快速流逝。

揭示**正常感知中不可见的模式**——云彩飞驰、花朵绽放、城市昼夜脉动。

- 相关: [快动作](taxonomy:225) | [常速](taxonomy:227)

tutorial.en:
# Slow-Motion

A slow-motion video with forward playback speed slower than real-time. Events unfold **more slowly than they occurred**, revealing details invisible at normal speed.

Slow-motion is one of cinema's most powerful temporal tools, used for **emphasizing dramatic moments, revealing beauty in fast action, conveying emotional weight, or creating dreamlike atmosphere**. It is achieved by filming at a higher frame rate than playback (e.g., shooting at 120fps, playing at 24fps).

Sam Peckinpah's balletic slow-motion violence in [*The Wild Bunch* (1969)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wild_Bunch) and the Wachowskis' bullet-time in [*The Matrix* (1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix) are landmark uses of the technique.

- Related: [Regular Speed](taxonomy:227) | [Speed-Ramp](taxonomy:229) | [Fast-Motion](taxonomy:225)
tutorial.zh:
# 慢动作

前进播放速度慢于实时。通过以高帧率拍摄（如120fps拍、24fps放）实现。

用于**强调戏剧性时刻、展现快速动作中的美感或营造梦幻氛围**。[《黑客帝国》(1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix)的子弹时间是标志性范例。

- 相关: [常速](taxonomy:227) | [变速](taxonomy:229) | [快动作](taxonomy:225)

tutorial.en:
# Speed-Ramp

The video shows a speed ramp effect, where playback speed changes between faster and slower rates. The temporal flow **accelerates and decelerates** within the same shot, creating a dynamic rhythm.

Speed ramping became a signature technique of Zack Snyder in [*300* (2006)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/300_(film)), where combat would suddenly shift between normal speed, slow-motion, and accelerated motion. The technique creates **visceral emphasis on impact moments** by slowing down at the point of contact and speeding up through transitions.

- Related: [Slow-Motion](taxonomy:228) | [Fast-Motion](taxonomy:225)
tutorial.zh:
# 变速

播放速度在快慢之间变化，在同一镜头内**加速和减速**。

扎克·施奈德在[《300勇士》(2006)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/300_(film))中将其发展为标志性技法——在**撞击瞬间减速、过渡动作中加速**。

- 相关: [慢动作](taxonomy:228) | [快动作](taxonomy:225)

tutorial.en:
# Stop-Motion

A stop-motion video using frame-by-frame changes to simulate motion. Objects are **physically manipulated between individually photographed frames**, creating the illusion of movement when played in sequence.

Stop-motion is one of the oldest animation techniques, pioneered by Willis O'Brien in [*King Kong* (1933)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Kong_(1933_film)) and refined by Ray Harryhausen. Modern studios like [Aardman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations) (*Wallace & Gromit*) and Laika (*Coraline*, *Kubo*) continue to push the art form. The technique's inherent **tactile, handcrafted quality** gives it a charm distinct from digital animation.

- Related: [Time-Lapse](taxonomy:231)
tutorial.zh:
# 定格动画

通过逐帧改变物体位置来模拟运动。物体在**逐帧拍摄的照片之间被物理移动**。

最古老的动画技术之一，其**手工制作的触感**赋予它有别于数字动画的独特魅力。

- 相关: [延时摄影](taxonomy:231)

tutorial.en:
# Regular Speed

The playback is forward at real-time speed without noticeable speed-up or slowdown. The video runs at **normal temporal cadence**, matching how events occurred in reality.

Regular speed is the baseline of filmmaking. Any deviation from it (slow-motion, fast-motion, time-lapse, reverse) is a deliberate creative choice that draws attention. Regular speed feels transparent and naturalistic.

- Related: [Fast-Motion](taxonomy:225) | [Slow-Motion](taxonomy:228)
tutorial.zh:
# 常速

以实时速度前进播放，没有明显的加速或减速。

常速是电影制作的基准，任何偏离都是有意识的创作选择。

- 相关: [快动作](taxonomy:225) | [慢动作](taxonomy:228)

tutorial.en: A fast-motion video with forward playback speed moderately faster than real-time (about 1.5×3×), but not a time-lapse where the speed is greatly accelerated over a long duration.

# Time-Reversed

A time-reversed video where events play backward in time. The temporal flow is **inverted**, making effects precede causes, objects un-fall, and actions un-happen.

Reverse playback creates **surreal, disorienting, or poetic effects**. It can convey memory, magical reversal, or philosophical commentary on cause and effect. Music videos frequently use reverse playback for striking visual choreography.

- Related: [Regular Speed](taxonomy:227)
tutorial.zh:
# 倒放

事件倒序播放。时间流动被反转，使结果先于原因。

制造**超现实的效果**。

- 相关: [常速](taxonomy:227)

tutorial.en:
# Fast-Motion

A fast-motion video where playback is forward and moderately faster than real-time (about 1.5x to 3x). Motion appears **slightly to noticeably accelerated** but events remain comprehensible.

Fast-motion at moderate speeds is used for **comedic effect, conveying urgency, compressing routine activities, or adding energy** to otherwise mundane footage. It is distinct from time-lapse, which uses far greater acceleration (more than 3x) over longer periods.

- Related: [Time-Lapse](taxonomy:231) | [Regular Speed](taxonomy:227) | [Slow-Motion](taxonomy:228)
tutorial.zh:
# 快动作

前进播放且速度适度加快（约1.5至3倍），运动**略微到明显加快**但事件仍可辨认。

用于**喜剧效果、传达紧迫感或压缩日常活动**。与延时摄影不同，后者使用远大于3倍的加速。

- 相关: [延时摄影](taxonomy:231) | [常速](taxonomy:227) | [慢动作](taxonomy:228)

tutorial.en:
# Fisheye Distortion

The video shows extreme fisheye lens distortion, where most lines curve strongly outward. A **fisheye lens** produces a hemispherical or ultra-wide-angle view with pronounced barrel distortion, bending straight lines into curves.

Fisheye lenses are used for **skateboarding and action sports videos** (where the wide angle captures the full trick), artistic distortion, security camera aesthetics, and VR/360-degree content. The exaggerated perspective creates a **bubble-like view** that draws the center of the frame forward while warping the periphery.

- Related: [Overlays](taxonomy:116)
tutorial.zh:
# 鱼眼畸变

画面呈现极端鱼眼镜头畸变，直线强烈向外弯曲。

常用于**滑板和极限运动视频**（鱼眼能捕捉完整动作）以及VR/360度内容。

- 相关: [画面叠加](taxonomy:116)

tutorial.en:
# Frame Freeze

A video that contains a frame freeze effect at some point. A single frame is **held motionless** while the rest of the video continues in motion, creating a sudden temporal pause.

Frame freezes punctuate moments of **emphasis, humor, shock, or narrative commentary**. The classic freeze-frame ending, where the final shot holds on a character's expression, was popularized by [*The 400 Blows* (1959)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_400_Blows) and has been a staple ever since. Martin Scorsese uses freeze-frames with voice-over narration throughout [*Goodfellas*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas).

- Related: [Motion Blur](taxonomy:40)
tutorial.zh:
# 定格

画面中某处出现定格效果——某一帧被静止保持。

用于标点般地强调**重要时刻、幽默或震惊**。[《四百击》(1959)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_400_Blows)的定格结尾是影史经典。

- 相关: [运动模糊](taxonomy:40)

tutorial.en:
# Motion Blur

The video exhibits a motion blur effect. Moving objects or the camera itself produce **streaked, smeared imagery** due to exposure during movement, creating a sense of speed and fluidity.

Motion blur is a natural optical phenomenon that occurs when subjects move during the camera's exposure time. In cinema, it contributes to the smooth, filmic look of 24fps footage (typically shot at 1/48s shutter speed). Filmmakers can **exaggerate motion blur** with slow shutter speeds for dreamlike or disorienting effects, or **minimize it** with fast shutter speeds for the staccato look seen in [*Saving Private Ryan*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving_Private_Ryan).

- Related: [Fast Moving Camera](taxonomy:56) | [Frame Freeze](taxonomy:39)
tutorial.zh:
# 运动模糊

移动的物体或相机产生**条纹状、涂抹状的画面**。

运动模糊是24fps电影感的重要因素。可以通过慢速快门来增强运动模糊，营造梦幻或令人迷失方向的效果，也可以通过快速快门来减弱运动模糊。

- 相关: [快速运镜](taxonomy:56) | [定格](taxonomy:39)

tutorial.en:
# Overlays

A shot containing on-screen overlays, such as watermarks, titles, subtitles, icons, heads-up displays (HUDs), or framing elements. **Graphical elements are composited on top** of the underlying footage.

Overlays serve both practical and creative purposes: subtitles aid accessibility, HUDs provide gaming information, watermarks protect intellectual property, and title cards convey narrative information. In creative filmmaking, overlays like text, graphics, and AR-style elements can **blend diegetic and non-diegetic information** for innovative storytelling.

- Related: [Screen Recording POV](taxonomy:170)
tutorial.zh:
# 画面叠加

镜头中包含屏幕叠加元素——水印、标题、字幕、图标、HUD或画面框架元素。

兼具实用和创意目的。

- 相关: [屏幕录制视角](taxonomy:170)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Transition

The video includes a shot transition. The footage contains a **visual break between two distinct shots**, whether through a hard cut, dissolve, fade, wipe, or other transition effect.

Shot transitions are the fundamental building blocks of film editing. A **hard cut** provides instant change, a **dissolve** suggests passage of time, a **fade to black** signals a scene ending, and creative transitions like **wipes and match cuts** connect scenes thematically. The grammar of transitions has been developed over more than a century of cinema.

- Related: [Frame Freeze](taxonomy:39)
tutorial.zh:
# 转场

画面中存在两个不同镜头之间的视觉断点——硬切、溶解、淡出、擦除或其他转场效果。

转场是电影剪辑的基本构成单元。

- 相关: [定格](taxonomy:39)
